signals.review_reason: Single but critical: the application crashes immediately on startup for any user doing a fresh Docker install of agno 2.6.x. The error is reproducible, blocks the main entry point (`from agno.playground import Playground`), and requires manually adding `packaging` as an explicit dependency as a workaround. This is a main-flow startup阻断 for new users and fresh deployments.

signals.topic: GeminiInteractions: GenerateContentConfig not supported and auto-history merge broken
signals.summary: When using GeminiInteractions as the model provider, users cannot pass GenerateContentConfig for advanced control parameters, and the automatic history merging feature does not work — meaning multi-turn context is lost even when add_history_to_context=True.
signals.review_reason: Issue #7970 clearly documents two distinct functional failures with GeminiInteractions: (1) GenerateContentConfig cannot be passed, blocking advanced parameter control; (2) auto-history merging into cloud storage does not work, breaking multi-turn conversations even when explicitly enabled. Both are clear user-facing feature failures that degrade the Gemini model integration significantly.

signals.topic: TeamMode.route with store_tool_messages=False causes duplicate questions in multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: When a Team is set to TeamMode.route with max_tool_calls_from_history=0 or store_tool_messages=False, previous user questions are reused as input in subsequent turns, leading to duplicate processing of the same questions. The same config works correctly in TeamMode.coordinate.
signals.review_reason: Issue #7971 provides a full reproducible code example showing that in TeamMode.route with the specified config, the first user question is fed as input again when asking the second question — clearly visible in the conversation logs attached to the issue. This is a distinct workflow failure in multi-turn conversations that causes duplicate/unnecessary processing.

signals.topic: AgentOS multi-replica deployments: scheduler HTTP calls fail with 401 Unauthorized due to non-deterministic internal_service_token
signals.summary: AgentOS with multiple replicas (Railway default: 2) or workers (AWS uvicorn: 2) causes scheduler HTTP calls between replicas to fail with 401 Unauthorized because each process generates a different internal_service_token at startup. The token is stored in process-local memory, not shared. This silently breaks the scheduler feature in all production multi-replica deployments.
signals.review_reason: Issue #7954 documents a high-impact auth failure: when AgentOS runs with multiple replicas (the default on Railway) or workers (the default on AWS), scheduler HTTP calls silently fail with 401 because each process generates a different token. The issue describes the root cause clearly (per-process token generation), identifies the affected production templates (Railway, AWS, Docker), and notes the scheduler silently fails. The issue was closed with the fix accepted, confirming the bug existed.

signals.topic: Custom provider names hallucinated by model; system prompt omits friendly provider display name
signals.summary: When using providers with unfamiliar IDs (not anthropic/openai/fireworks), the system prompt renders the raw provider ID but not the friendly name. The model has nothing to anchor on and hallucinates provider names, causing incorrect commit messages to include wrong provider/model placeholders.
aliases: system prompt missing friendly provider name
signals.review_reason: Produces incorrect output (wrong commit messages with placeholder values). Verified with specific provider/model combination. Causes users to publish commits with incorrect metadata. Count=2 (duplicate reports). P1 due to output corruption rather than complete blockage.

source_issues.title: system prompt omits friendly provider name, hallucinates on unfamiliar ids
source_issues.evidence: System prompt renders raw ID 'neuralwatt/zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8' without friendly name; model copies AGENTS.md placeholder values verbatim into commit messages.

source_issues.title: system prompt omits friendly provider name, hallucinates on unfamiliar ids
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #28244. Same root cause: custom provider IDs not anchored in system prompt, causing model hallucination of provider names.

signals.topic: Bun segfault (panic in drainMicrotasks) when opencode attach --dir has no matching session
signals.summary: opencode attach with --dir pointing to a directory with no matching server session causes Bun to segfault/crash instead of showing a friendly error. Reproduces reliably across OS versions and terminals. Blocks the attach workflow entirely.
signals.review_reason: App crash (segfault) that reliably blocks the 'opencode attach' workflow entirely. Users see 'Bun has crashed' instead of a friendly error. Clear stack trace and reproducible steps. P0 due to complete workflow blockage with confirmed crash evidence.

source_issues.title: opencode attach segfaults (Bun panic in drainMicrotasks) when --dir has no matching session
source_issues.evidence: Bun segmentation fault at address 0x103EE1B5C; panic in Bun::jsFunctionDrainMicrotaskQueue. Reproduces with and without PTY on macOS. Consistent crash hash across runs.

signals.topic: Session renderer crashes when reasoning part has undefined text
signals.summary: ReasoningPartDisplay calls .trim() on potentially undefined text without a fallback, causing TypeError when viewing sessions with malformed/incomplete reasoning parts. Session UI crashes instead of gracefully handling the data.
aliases: session renderer crash undefined text trim
signals.review_reason: App crash that blocks viewing of session history. TypeError in session renderer causes complete UI crash. Identified root cause in source code (missing ?? '' guard before .trim()). Blocks a core workflow (reviewing past sessions).

source_issues.title: Session renderer crashes when reasoning part has undefined text
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim') in ReasoningPartDisplay at packages/ui/src/components/message-part.tsx. Crashes session viewing for sessions with malformed reasoning parts.

signals.topic: Composer draft text is lost when a permission prompt appears mid-session
signals.summary: When a permission prompt is triggered during an active AI session, the composer input component is unmounted via SolidJS <Show> and the user's typed draft is destroyed. After dismissing the permission, the composer remounts empty — typed text is permanently lost.
signals.review_reason: Direct data loss — users lose typed work when permission prompts interrupt their flow. This is a confirmed component unmount bug in SolidJS that destroys unsaved state. Repeated scenario in normal usage. Clear user impact: work disappears.

source_issues.title: Composer draft is lost when a permission prompt appears mid-session
source_issues.evidence: SolidJS <Show when={!blocked()}> unmounts composer on permission prompt; draft text destroyed. After allow/dismiss, composer remounts empty. No persistence of typed content.

signals.topic: Windows: session list disappears after refresh in opencode web due to mixed path separators
signals.summary: On Windows, opencode web mixes forward and backward slashes in session paths. After a refresh, sessions vanish because the path comparison fails. Users lose track of active sessions on every refresh.
aliases: windows session list disappears path slash
opencode web windows session refresh lost
signals.review_reason: Windows platform issue causing session list to disappear on refresh — a core workflow on Windows is broken. Users cannot reliably manage sessions. Clear reproduction path. P0 despite count=1 due to complete Windows workflow blockage.

source_issues.title: On windows we have a problem with 'opencode web' because forward and backward slashes are mixed up
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 user: sessions visible briefly after restart then disappear on refresh. Path slash mismatch causes session list mismatch.

signals.topic: Files list API 无法在 Managed Agent API 上下文中列出文件，用户无法覆盖 beta header
signals.summary: Managed Agent API 场景下 Files list API 无法使用，因 FileServiceImpl 固定添加默认 beta header，缺少 managed-agents-2026-04-01，且无 header 覆盖机制，导致用户无法列出管理代理上下文中的文件。
aliases: Files list API missing managed agent support
无法在 managed agent 上下文列出文件
signals.review_reason: 用户明确指出 Files list API 在 Managed Agent API 场景下不可用，根因是 FileServiceImpl 硬编码 beta header 缺少 managed-agents-2026-04-01，且无 override 机制，导致用户无法完成文件列表查询这一常见操作，属于主流程功能阻断性缺陷。count=1 故降级为 P1，不满足 P0 的高频要求。

source_issues.title: Files list API does not support listing files from managed agent API
source_issues.evidence: FileServiceImpl 在 listFiles 时固定添加默认 beta header，缺少 managed-agents-2026-04-01，用户无法覆盖该 header，导致在 Managed Agent API 下无法列出文件，属于主流程功能阻断。

signals.topic: Managed agents: vault_ids credentials not inherited by subagents, breaking MCP OAuth calls in multi-agent patterns
signals.summary: When a coordinator agent dispatches a subagent via agent_toolset_20260401, vault credentials configured via vault_ids at sessions.create are not available to the subagent. Any MCP tool call in the subagent requiring OAuth credentials silently fails or returns auth errors. This blocks the primary use case of multi-agent orchestrated pipelines that need external API access from subagents.
aliases: vault_ids not passed to subagent tool calls
MCP OAuth fails in managed agents subagent dispatch
signals.review_reason: Subagent MCP OAuth calls fail silently in multi-agent managed-agent patterns, completely blocking the documented secure vault+MCP integration use case when using coordinator/subagent splits. The only workaround (manual multi-session orchestration) abandons the agent_toolset abstraction entirely.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents: vault_ids not inherited by subagents dispatched via agent_toolset — MCP OAuth calls fail
source_issues.evidence: vault_ids only exists on sessions.create; agent_toolset_20260401 accepts no vault_ids parameter; subagent MCP calls fail with auth errors while coordinator's own MCP calls succeed with the same vault credential; confirmed workaround of separate sessions per agent works but defeats agent_toolset purpose

signals.topic: Prompt caching: server writes unrequested cache entries past explicit breakpoint, billing 1.25x for tokens never read
signals.summary: On warm calls with only a system-level cache_control breakpoint, the server writes an additional ~1416 cache tokens at the user content boundary. These writes are billed at 1.25x cache-write rate but never produce cache reads on subsequent calls, since the content past the breakpoint varies per request. This directly contradicts documented behavior and causes measurable cost loss.
aliases: cache_control writes extra entries beyond breakpoint
uncalled cache writes on warm calls
signals.review_reason: Users are billed 1.25x for cache writes that produce zero cache read benefit. This is a direct cost loss for users who opt into explicit (non-automatic) caching with a single breakpoint. The server-side behavior contradicts documented contract, and no opt-out mechanism exists.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Server writes additional cache entries past explicit cache_control breakpoint, billing 1.25x for tokens that are never read
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced across SDK versions 0.79.0 to 0.102.0; Call 2/3 show cache_creation=1416 on warm calls despite only one cache_control marker; documented behavior states only one entry written at breakpoint; billed at 1.25x cache-write rate with zero cache read benefit

signals.topic: files.beta.upload: deepcopy_minimal mutates input dict in place when FileTypes tuple contains a Mapping, corrupting caller data
signals.summary: deepcopy_minimal in files.beta.upload does not recursively copy tuples, only lists and dicts. When a FileTypes tuple's 4th element (a Mapping such as a headers dict) is mutated in place by the upload process, the original caller's dict is corrupted. This silently corrupts user data structures with no error raised.
aliases: deepcopy_minimal tuple mutation in file upload
FileTypes tuple dict mutation side effect
signals.review_reason: The SDK silently mutates the caller's input data structure. No error is raised, so users may not notice the corruption until downstream code fails with unexpected state. This is a data corruption defect that affects any caller using FileTypes tuples with a Mapping element.

source_issues.title: Use of deepcopy_minimal in files.beta.upload mutates dict in place
source_issues.evidence: Empirically confirmed: headers dict within FileTypes tuple is modified in place and returned to caller changed; deepcopy_minimal at src/anthropic/_utils/_utils.py#L187 does not recurse into tuples; user was unaware their data was corrupted until they noticed the mutation

signals.topic: Token counting not supported on Bedrock despite being listed as supported in platform documentation
signals.summary: AnthropicBedrock client throws AnthropicError 'Token counting is not supported in Bedrock yet', but the official platform documentation at platform.claude.ai states that token counting is supported on all third-party platform APIs including Bedrock. This is a documentation-implementation mismatch that misleads users.
aliases: Bedrock count_tokens not implemented despite docs
AnthropicBedrock token counting unsupported but documented
signals.review_reason: Feature advertised in documentation as available on Bedrock is actually unsupported, causing user confusion and broken workflows. While not billing-impacting, it causes predictable runtime failures for Bedrock users who follow documented API parity.

source_issues.title: Token counting is not supported in Bedrock yet
source_issues.evidence: Client throws AnthropicError on count_tokens call; docs at platform.claude.ai enumerate token counting as supported on third-party platform APIs; user reports confusion between documented capability and actual behavior

signals.topic: Message batch processing: custom_id undocumented 64-character limit causes BadRequestError on submit
signals.summary: Passing a custom_id longer than 64 characters to message batch requests results in a BadRequestError (400). The error message is clear ('String should have at most 64 characters') but this limit is not documented anywhere in the Anthropic API documentation. Users must discover this constraint only through trial and error, leading to failed batch submissions and wasted dev time.
aliases: message batch custom_id length constraint missing from docs
signals.review_reason: Undocumented API constraint causes predictable BadRequestError failures for users submitting message batches. The limit is purely a documentation gap — the error is clear but users should not have to discover this by trial and error when building batch processing workflows.

source_issues.title: Message Batch Processing - undocumented character limit for custom_id parameter
source_issues.evidence: Submitting custom_id with 65 characters produces BadRequestError; limit of 64 not documented in API docs or SDK; confirmed by user searching documentation and code review

signals.topic: TypeScript type error: Cannot access `.text` property on `ContentBlock` after SDK upgrade
signals.summary: After upgrading from v0.20.9 to v0.22.0, TypeScript users encounter a type error (`Property 'text' does not exist on type 'ContentBlock'`) when accessing `msg.content[0].text`. This blocks type-safe access to message content and forces users to use `// @ts-ignore` as a workaround.
aliases: TypeScript type narrowing for message content blocks
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: a TypeScript version regression that forces users to add `// @ts-ignore` workarounds to access message content text. While it does not fully block the API call itself, it breaks developer experience, requires code changes, and is a regression from a prior version. The issue has 9 comments indicating community interest, and the user explicitly describes it as blocking type-safe code. Count=1 so priority is P2, not P0.

source_issues.title: [Types] Error: Property 'text' does not exist on type 'ContentBlock'.
source_issues.evidence: User reports type error after upgrading SDK version. Code works at runtime but TypeScript rejects `msg.content[0].text` as a type error. User is forced to add `// @ts-ignore` as a workaround.

signals.topic: Bundled CLI hangs when stdout is not a TTY, blocking CI/CD, Docker, and headless environments
signals.summary: The bundled `claude` binary hangs indefinitely when stdout is a pipe, file, or non-TTY device, making the SDK unusable in CI runners, Docker containers without -t, launchd/cron jobs, and other standard production environments. The hang is silent with no diagnostic output.
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow blocker for any production deployment that captures stdout (CI, Docker, orchestrators, cron). The hang is silent and total — no error, no progress, requiring kill. This is not cosmetic; it makes the SDK unusable in standard production environments.

source_issues.title: Bundled `claude` binary hangs when stdout is not a TTY (pipe / file / launchd / cron / Docker)
source_issues.evidence: Any Python script that uses claude_agent_sdk hangs indefinitely when its stdout is a pipe or a regular file. CI runners, launchd/cron jobs, and Docker containers without -t are all affected — the symptom is silent hang with no diagnostic output.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely after subprocess shutdown handler blocks
signals.summary: When running ~200 parallel Claude Code instances via the SDK, 30% of jobs hang indefinitely after successful completion because the transport.close() never returns, causing VM infrastructure timeouts.
signals.review_reason: This causes 30% of parallel production jobs to hang indefinitely after successful completion. The job is done but the transport never closes, causing VM infrastructure timeouts. Direct cost impact: workers become unavailable and runs fail at infrastructure level.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely if subprocess shutdown handler blocks
source_issues.evidence: In our use case (running ~200 parallel Claude Code instances via the SDK), 30% of jobs hung indefinitely — Claude Code job finished successfully but the VM stayed hanging because the SDK's transport.close() never returned, causing the entire worker process to hit VM infra timeout.

signals.topic: CLI failures produce unhelpful 'Command failed with exit code 1' with no actual stderr or typed exception
signals.summary: When the Claude CLI subprocess exits with a non-zero code, the SDK destroys all error context through exception flattening. Consumer code that catches ClaudeSDKError never fires. The error message says 'Check stderr output for details' but stderr is hardcoded and never captured.
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow failure that makes debugging CLI errors impossible. All error context (actual stderr output, typed exceptions, exit codes) is systematically stripped, leaving users with 'Command failed with exit code 1' and no way to diagnose what happened. Every CLI error is a dead end.

source_issues.title: Error context destroyed through exception flattening — CLI failures produce unhelpful 'Command failed with exit code 1'
source_issues.evidence: When the Claude CLI subprocess exits with a non-zero code, the SDK destroys all error context through a 3-step chain. Consumer code that catches ClaudeSDKError never fires. The error message says 'Check stderr output for details' but stderr is hardcoded and never captured. No actionable detail reaches the user.

signals.topic: Stderr callback error permanently kills stderr delivery for rest of session
signals.summary: When the user-provided options.stderr callback raises even once, the exception is silently caught, the stderr loop terminates, and no further stderr lines are delivered for the remainder of the session. A single buggy stderr line permanently disables stderr piping.
signals.review_reason: A single stderr callback error permanently disables all subsequent stderr output for the remainder of the session. Subsequent CLI errors that would otherwise reach the user's logger are silently lost. The failure is silent (no log, no traceback), making debugging impossible.

source_issues.title: Bug: stderr callback raise silently kills _handle_stderr loop, dropping all subsequent stderr lines
source_issues.evidence: When the user-provided options.stderr callback raises (even once), the exception is caught at the outer level, the loop terminates, and no further stderr lines are delivered for the rest of the session. The except Exception: pass is silent — the user has no way to know their callback errored.

signals.topic: Premature TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running, causing cascade of wasted work
signals.summary: The orchestrator receives premature task-notification while subagent is still running (13 of 39 tools). This caused 5 reviewer subagents to be dispatched against non-existent files, the orchestrator re-dispatched all 5 researchers (~8 min wasted), totaling 32 min and $21.51 in duplicate work.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure with direct cost impact. Premature notifications cause the orchestrator to make incorrect decisions (dispatching downstream agents against non-existent files), triggering wasted computation (8+ minutes of duplicate work per incident). Non-deterministic and hard to reproduce, making it particularly insidious in production.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: The orchestrator received premature task-notification while subagent was still at tool=13 of its eventual 39 tools. Premature notifications caused: 5 reviewer subagents dispatched against output files that didn't exist yet; orchestrator re-dispatched all 5 researchers (~8 min wasted); total run wasted 32 min and $21.51 in duplicate work.

signals.topic: Isolation flags (mcpServers:{}, settingSources:[], skills:[]) fail to prevent operator context leaking into SDK init payload, bloating prompt 200–400KB and causing response compaction
signals.summary: When a host program passes documented isolation flags mcpServers:{}, settingSources:[], and skills:[], the SDK's system.init event still ships the operator's full claude.ai connector inventory (87–369 MCP tools), connected servers, agents, memory_paths.auto, and skills. This prevents bounded sub-agent calls from getting a clean init payload and causes compacted_lost_tool_use escalations on calls that should fit comfortably in context budget.
signals.review_reason: The documented isolation contract is violated: passing mcpServers:{}, settingSources:[], and skills:[] still leaks 87–369 operator tools plus agents/skills/memory_paths into init. This directly causes response compaction in bounded sub-agent workflows, a clear operational blocker for production embedding. Strong evidence with detailed repro and measured bloat.

source_issues.title: Options { mcpServers: {}, settingSources: [], skills: [] } doesn't strip claude.ai-connector tools, agents, or memory_paths.auto from system init (0.2.126)
source_issues.evidence: Repro shows expected ~1 tool but observed 88–370 tools, 0 agents but observed 6, 0 skills but observed 8, undefined memory_paths.auto but observed populated. Prompt bloat is 200–400KB. Response compaction events observed with compacted_lost_tool_use escalation reason.

signals.topic: Native binary distribution (~230MB) exceeds Vercel 250MB and Lambda function size limits, blocking serverless deployment with no documented workaround
signals.summary: Since v0.2.110 the SDK ships a Bun-compiled single-executable (~230MB) as optionalDependencies. This exceeds Vercel's 250MB function size cap and Lambda's 250MB unzipped layer limit by itself, before any application code. Downgrade to pre-native JS bundle is blocked because the skills API (needed by many users) was introduced after v0.2.109. No documented path exists for serverless deployment.
signals.review_reason: The native binary at ~230MB demonstrably exceeds Vercel's 250MB hard limit and Lambda's unzipped cap, making serverless deployment a confirmed blocker for two major platforms. The downgrade path is also closed due to skills API dependency. This is a critical deployment-path failure with no documented workaround.

source_issues.title: Native binary distribution (≥0.2.110) makes Agent SDK unusable in Vercel/Lambda serverless deployments (230 MB pushes past the 250 MB function size cap)
source_issues.evidence: Deploying to Vercel with @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.2.138 fails with 'Native CLI binary for linux-x64 not found'. Adding outputFileTracingIncludes surfaces the 230MB binary, which alone exceeds the 250MB limit. JS bundle (last at v0.2.109) is ~13MB but lacks the skills API introduced at v0.2.120.

signals.topic: OTel tracer emits bare token attribute names instead of GenAI semconv names, breaking downstream cost tracking in Langfuse and similar observability tools
signals.summary: The bundled OTel tracer (scope com.anthropic.claude_code.tracing v1.0.0) emits token counts under bare names (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens) instead of the OTel GenAI semantic convention names (gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, etc.). Downstream observability platforms like Langfuse auto-extract cost from semconv attribute names and receive no token data, pricing every generation at $0.
signals.review_reason: The tracer diverges from OTel GenAI semconv, causing downstream cost extraction to fail silently (all generations priced at $0 in Langfuse). This is a direct billing/cost visibility loss for production users relying on observability tooling, not just a spec-compliance issue. Clear downstream impact evidence with concrete Langfuse observations.

source_issues.title: Tracer emits non-semconv token attributes (scope com.anthropic.claude_code.tracing v1.0.0) — continuation of #304 with new evidence
source_issues.evidence: Langfuse shows usage_details: {} and calculated_total_cost: $0.0 for every generation despite correct model registry. The four token-count attributes use bare names instead of gen_ai.usage.* prefix. Parent-process SpanProcessor workaround fails because SDK CLI runs as child process with its own OTLP export.

signals.topic: restoreConfigFromBase/cpSync ENOENT crashes on dangling or broken symlinks in .claude/ and SENSITIVE_PATHS
signals.summary: When CI workspaces contain dangling symlinks (e.g. CLAUDE.md → deleted file, .claude/ → moved directory), the action crashes at restoreConfigFromBase or during "Restoring sensitive files" with ENOENT. This blocks the entire PR workflow for affected repos. Multiple regression since v1.0.89 with no permanent fix.
signals.review_reason: 5 confirmed bugs across 2 code paths (restoreConfigFromBase + cpSync), all causing ENOENT crashes on symlinks. Main workflow is completely blocked for any CI workspace containing symlinks — a common pattern in monorepos and Docker environments. Regression confirmed across multiple v1 releases with no permanent fix, indicating systemic issue.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase ENOENT on .claude/ symlinks whose target is outside SENSITIVE_PATHS (regression after dereference + Bun 1.3.14)
source_issues.evidence: Crashes with ENOENT when snapshot contains symlink whose target lives outside SENSITIVE_PATHS. Regression after Bun 1.3.14 + dereference change.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase crashes on dangling symlinks in .claude/ directory
source_issues.evidence: restoreConfigFromBase fails with ENOENT when .claude/skills/ contains symlinks whose targets don't exist at action runtime.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase crashes with ENOENT when only CLAUDE.md exists (cpSync needs mkdir of .claude-pr/ first)
source_issues.evidence: ENOENT crash when head has CLAUDE.md but no .claude directory. cpSync fails because .claude-pr/ dir not created first.

source_issues.title: cpSync fails on symlinked sensitive files
source_issues.evidence: v1 tag fails with ENOENT during 'Restoring sensitive files from origin/master' when any SENSITIVE_PATHS entry is a symlink.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Since v1.0.89, action crashes during restoreConfigFromBase when SENSITIVE_PATHS (CLAUDE.md etc.) is a symlink.

signals.topic: Bot actors (GitHub Copilot, scheduled workflows) cause 404 Not Found errors in permission/actor checks, preventing allowed_bots from working
signals.summary: checkHumanActor and checkWritePermissions both call GitHub APIs with non-user actor names (Copilot SWE agent, bot accounts). These calls return 404, crashing the action before allowed_bots configuration is even evaluated. This blocks entire class of automation-triggered workflows.
signals.review_reason: 4 confirmed bugs across 2 validation functions (checkHumanActor + checkWritePermissions) both producing 404 for bot actors. This is a systemic architectural flaw: the allowed_bots feature is designed to handle bot actors but crashes before it can evaluate the config. Workflows triggered by Copilot, scheduled bots, or any non-user actor fail completely.

source_issues.title: Action fails with 'Not Found' when triggered by GitHub Copilot (actor Copilot returns 404 from /users/ API)
source_issues.evidence: checkHumanActor crashes with 404 for GitHub Copilot SWE agent (actor='Copilot'), preventing allowed_bots from taking effect. Action completely fails for Copilot-triggered workflows.

source_issues.title: allowed_bots bypasses actor check but not permission check — bot actors still fail with 404
source_issues.evidence: allowed_bots bypasses checkHumanActor but not checkWritePermissions. Bot actors still fail with 404 on the permissions check, blocking bot-triggered workflows.

source_issues.title: checkWritePermissions fails with 404 for non-user actors like 'Copilot'
source_issues.evidence: checkWritePermissions calls getCollaboratorPermissionLevel with github.actor (bot name), which returns 404 for non-user accounts, crashing the action.

source_issues.title: checkHumanActor fails with 404 for bot actors before checking allowed_bots configuration
source_issues.evidence: checkHumanActor fails with 404 for scheduled workflows and bot actors before allowed_bots configuration is even checked, making allowed_bots ineffective.

signals.topic: Branch name validation (validateBranchName) rejects valid GitHub branch names containing # or commas, causing workflow validation failures
signals.summary: The validateBranchName function uses overly strict regex that rejects characters GitHub and git permit in branch names (#, commas). Workflows fail validation for any PR with such branches, blocking the entire CI run.
signals.review_reason: Workflow validation is a pre-execution gate. Rejecting valid GitHub branch names blocks the entire CI run for affected PRs. This is a clear false positive in validation logic — the function is more restrictive than GitHub itself.

source_issues.title: workflow validation failed if base branch's name has # in it
source_issues.evidence: PRs with base branch names containing '#' fail with 'workflow validation failed'. The action's branch validation is stricter than GitHub's own acceptance criteria.

source_issues.title: validateBranchName() rejects branch names containing a comma (,)
source_issues.evidence: validateBranchName() rejects branch names with commas even though git check-ref-format permits them and GitHub accepts them.

signals.topic: execution_file output not written when SDK throws error_max_turns — execution data (messages, cost, turn count, duration) silently lost
signals.summary: When Claude Code hits the max turns limit, the SDK throws and the execution_file output is never written to disk. Users lose all execution data for rate-limited or long-running tasks, which is critical for CI/CD billing and debugging.
aliases: execution_file not written on max turns
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss on a common scenario (max turns). Users cannot audit cost, debug failures, or get any output when Claude Code hits turn limits — a scenario that occurs frequently in CI. This is a clear critical-function unavailability issue, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: execution_file output not written when SDK throws on error_max_turns
source_issues.evidence: When Claude Code reaches maximum turns, the SDK throws error_max_turns. The execution_file output is not written to disk. Users lose all execution data (messages, cost, turn count, duration) — critical for CI billing and debugging.

signals.topic: .claude-pr/ snapshot directory accidentally committed to user PR branches when bot pushes fix commits

aliases: temp dir pushed to PR branch
signals.review_reason: Data integrity and cleanliness issue. Internal snapshot directory leaking into user PRs creates noise, potential exposure of sensitive paths, and confusing git history. While not a hard crash, it actively degrades the user experience every time the bot commits a fix.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase snapshot at .claude-pr/ gets committed to PR branch when bot pushes a fix
source_issues.evidence: .claude-pr/ snapshot directory created by restoreConfigFromBase is unintentionally committed to the user's PR branch whenever the Claude bot makes fix-up commits. This pollutes the PR with internal state files.

signals.topic: Voice hold mode: recording indicator appears before audio capture begins, dropping initial speech
signals.summary: Press-to-talk recording delay — indicator shows immediately but audio capture starts seconds later, losing words spoken in the gap. User must re-record or repeat content.
aliases: voice hold mode audio capture lag
signals.review_reason: Two related voice mode UI bugs. #60355: pressing hold-to-talk shows the recording indicator immediately but audio capture begins seconds later, causing the first words to be lost — this is a direct content loss bug that undermines the core voice input workflow. #60354: UI indicator persists in recording state after submission, creating a misleading/stuck UI state. Both confirmed on macOS with clear repro steps. Together they make voice hold mode unreliable for short utterances.

source_issues.title: Voice hold mode: recording starts seconds after indicator appears, dropping initial speech
source_issues.evidence: Indicator appears immediately but actual audio capture starts a few seconds later. Anything spoken in between is lost. Consistent repro on macOS.

source_issues.title: Voice indicator shows recording state after message is submitted
source_issues.evidence: After pressing Enter to submit, UI continues to display recording indicator despite mic being off. Separate but related: the indicator state is unreliable — appears late at start, clears late at end.

signals.topic: CCD desktop silently drops sessions on relaunch with no in-app recovery path
signals.summary: After relaunch (crash/power-loss/reboot), most sessions disappear from sidebar and Recents. JSONL data intact on disk but inaccessible through UI. CLI --resume works but sessions stay invisible to desktop sidebar.
signals.review_reason: A single-session bug but with severe and well-evidenced user impact: on relaunch, sessions vanish silently from the UI despite data being intact on disk. The user has no in-app path to recover — must use terminal commands. This directly blocks the primary use case (continuing work across restarts). Affects all platforms (reported on Windows, session management is core desktop functionality).

source_issues.title: [BUG] CCD desktop silently drops sessions on relaunch and has no in-app recovery; CLI --resume produces sessions invisible to the sidebar
source_issues.evidence: After power-loss, 5 of 6 sessions vanished from sidebar. JSONL files intact on disk. No UI to recover. CLI --resume works but pointer entrypoint:cli is filtered by desktop. No banner/toast/warning that sessions were dropped. User had to inspect filesystem to find JSONLs, then use cmd terminal to resume. Long-running 148MB/49K-turn session at risk of permanent loss.

signals.topic: Last user message floats as sticky overlay over chat history, blocking all content underneath
signals.summary: When scrolling up to review chat history, the most recent user message renders as a floating overlay covering the entire content area. Blocks reading of assistant responses, file panels, and command input. No way to dismiss.
signals.review_reason: UI overlay bug that makes chat history unreadable. The sticky overlay blocks all conversation content, side panels, and input area — completely preventing the user from reviewing prior context. No workaround. Confirmed with screenshot evidence. Significant UX degradation for any user reviewing multi-message sessions.

source_issues.title: Last user message overlays content when scrolling chat history
source_issues.evidence: After sending a multi-line message with optional image, scrolling up to review history causes the last user message to stick as a floating overlay. Overlay covers entire viewport blocking: previous assistant responses, right-side file/document panels, bottom command input area. Consistent repro, screenshot attached showing full viewport coverage.

signals.topic: Operator-curated auto-memory and CLAUDE.md act as cross-session priming inputs, causing internal vocabulary to leak into public artefacts (commit messages, PR descriptions)
signals.summary: Internal labels and process vocabulary accumulated in auto-memory/CLAUDE.md get loaded into new sessions as priming context, then emitted into public surfaces like commit messages and PR descriptions without user consent.
signals.review_reason: Memory feature actively causes user-visible quality defect: internal process labels leak into public-facing commit messages and PR descriptions, requiring manual scrubbing and force-push. The report documents that using the product's recommended feature (persistent memory) more rigorously worsens the bug. This is a systemic quality problem with a demonstrated real-world outcome (scrubbed commits, residual leakage in merged PRs).

source_issues.title: Operator-curated persistent artefacts act as cross-session priming inputs that produce vocabulary-leakage on fresh sessions
source_issues.evidence: User-curated auto-memory and CLAUDE.md loaded at fresh session start primed the model with internal parking-lot labels (PL #NN, Finding N, Watching Brief, pre-alpha review). Fresh session emitted these in commit messages on a public branch. Required force-push to scrub. Partial residual survived into merged PR body. The recommended feature (persistent memory) is the root cause — more sophisticated memory use creates denser priming and more reliable leakage. No operator-side mitigation works; in-loop corrections don't stop it.

signals.topic: Summarization cookbook notebook fails at cell 8 due to deprecated assistant message prefill causing BadRequestError
signals.summary: The `capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb` notebook breaks at cell 8 with a BadRequestError because it uses assistant message prefill, which has been deprecated. Users who follow the cookbook run into a blocking error and cannot complete the summarization tutorial.
aliases: assistant message prefill deprecation breaks summarization notebook
summarization guide notebook broken by API change
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with full stack trace. The notebook is part of the official cookbook collection — a primary learning resource. Users attempting to run it encounter a blocking BadRequestError at cell 8, which prevents them from completing the summarization tutorial. The issue is labeled 'bug' and has been active for 6 days with no resolution. Impact is clear: main learning path for summarization is broken.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Summarization cookbook fails due to use of assistant message prefill
source_issues.evidence: Cell 8 in `capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb` produces `BadRequestError: This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.` Users following the cookbook hit a blocking error and cannot proceed. Error trace confirmed against model claude-sonnet-4-6 with client library v0.XX.

signals.topic: Telegram split-reply chunks 2+ silently route to wrong topic in forum supergroups

source_issues.title: [telegram] split-reply chunks 2+ silently land in General topic of forum supergroup
source_issues.evidence: chunks 2+ lose reply_parameters and message_thread_id, silently land in wrong topic; General closed → error

signals.topic: README states Python 3.8+ requirement but code uses PEP 604 union syntax requiring Python 3.10+, causing TypeError on import for users on Python 3.8/3.9
signals.summary: The README.md for the agents quickstart advertises Python 3.8+ as the minimum requirement, but the source code uses PEP 604 union syntax (`X | None`) and PEP 585 generics (`list[...]`) which are only available in Python 3.10+. There is no `from __future__ import annotations` guard, so these annotations are evaluated at definition time. Users following the README and running on Python 3.8 or 3.9 hit `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'type' and 'NoneType'` immediately on `from agents.agent import Agent`.
aliases: PEP 604 syntax causes TypeError on Python 3.8/3.9
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: the README advertises a Python version that does not match what the code actually requires, causing a TypeError on import — a main-flow blocking failure. A user following the documented instructions will be unable to run the quickstart at all on Python 3.8 or 3.9. Marked P1 (not P0) because count=1 and it is single-repo, so lacks the multi-repo/high-frequency evidence required for P0.

source_issues.title: agents/README.md states "Python 3.8+" but code requires Python 3.10+ (PEP 604 union syntax)
source_issues.evidence: README advertises Python 3.8+; code in agents/agent.py uses `list[Tool] | None` syntax without `from __future__ import annotations`; CI runs Python 3.11.6; importing Agent on Python 3.8/3.9 raises TypeError immediately.

signals.topic: 课程"Structured Data"教授的预填充+停止序列技术已过时，与当前推荐的Structured Outputs冲突
signals.summary: 官方API课程的"Structured Data"课时仍在教授使用预填充assistant消息+停止序列来提取结构化JSON，该方法已被官方明确废弃，并与Structured Outputs不兼容。学习该课程的开发者会被引导采用过时且不推荐的实现模式。
aliases: deprecated prefill stop sequence technique taught in course
course material lagging behind current API best practice
signals.review_reason: Issue #161提供了明确的用户影响证据：课程教授的技术已被官方文档明确标记为与当前推荐方案不兼容，学员学完课程后会使用过时且次优的实现模式，导致实际开发中使用废弃的API调用方式。虽仅涉及单一仓库，但内容质量问题直接影响所有学习该课程的开发者的代码质量，构成实际用户痛点。

source_issues.title: [Content outdated] "Structured Data" lesson teaches prefill + stop sequences, superseded by structured outputs

signals.topic: API endpoint/model incompatibility causing tutorial to be non-functional
signals.summary: The tutorial uses outdated API endpoints or model identifiers that are no longer supported, causing the application to fail when users try to use it with current Claude models.
signals.review_reason: 用户主流程被直接阻断——API 无法正常工作，导致教程完全不可用。虽然 count=1，但用户提供了明确的影响证据（API 不可用、新模型无法选择、Claude 自身提示需要更新），属于关键功能不可用而非边缘问题。

source_issues.title: I Can't get it to take my API
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states they cannot select newer engines/models and the API does not work, preventing them from using the tutorial at all. Claude itself flagged that the code needs updating.

signals.topic: Skill tools that don't exist on the running platform fail silently with no error — cross-platform skill development is untestable
signals.summary: When a SKILL.md references a tool not available on the current platform, Claude silently falls back to prose or substitutes a different tool with incompatible semantics. Authors get zero signal that the skill ran differently than intended, making cross-platform skill development effectively untestable.
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking: cross-platform skill execution silently degrades with opposite behavior and no error signal. Authors cannot test skills across platforms — a core development workflow failure. Specific reproductions with concrete tool-name examples on two platforms.

source_issues.title: Skills referencing tools that don't exist on the running platform fail silently
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction A: 6 of 7 Claude.ai-only tools produced no error when run on Claude Code — prose fallback instead. Reproduction B: Claude.ai silently substituted create_file for Write with opposite overwrite semantics. Skills tested on one platform behave oppositely on the other with no error to author or user.

signals.topic: Skill's references/ relative paths resolve against process cwd instead of skill directory — skills can't load their own files
signals.summary: SKILL.md instructions to read files via relative paths like references/spec.md resolve against the Claude Code process CWD, not the skill's own directory. This causes all relative-file-reference skills to fail on both Claude Code (file-not-found) and Claude.ai (rejects relative paths outright).
aliases: relative path not resolved from skill dir
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking: skill-creator's own documented pattern (references/ progressive disclosure) is broken on both Claude Code and Claude.ai. Any skill attempting to load its own support files via relative paths will fail, breaking a core skill-authoring workflow.

source_issues.title: references/ relative paths don't resolve from the skill's directory
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code: 'File does not exist' — resolves against process cwd /Users/<user>/Documents/<project>. Claude.ai: 'references/spec.md is not an absolute path' — rejects relative paths outright. skill-creator SKILL.md recommends the references/ progressive-disclosure pattern, but it is broken by design.

signals.topic: skill-creator run_loop.py crashes between iterations when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent — inconsistent auth between eval and improve steps
signals.summary: The skill-creator run_loop.py crashes at improve_description.py because it constructs anthropic.Anthropic() directly (requiring ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) while the eval step uses claude -p subprocess (user subscription auth). Users with Claude Code subscription but no API key can run iteration 1 but crash immediately after, contradicting the SKILL.md's promise that the full flow runs via subscription.
aliases: skill optimizer crash without API key
improve step requires API key not documented
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking: the skill optimization loop crashes mid-workflow for any user without an API key, despite a Claude Code subscription. Complete reproduction with step-by-step repro. Contradicts the skill's own documented intent that the full flow runs via subscription.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop.py improve step crashes without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (inconsistent with eval step)
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction steps provided: authenticated Claude Code subscription user, no API key set, runs run_loop.py, iteration 1 completes, then crashes at client.messages.create() with TypeError about missing auth. The SKILL.md explicitly says to use the model from the system prompt implying subscription auth — yet improve step requires separate API key.

signals.topic: Embedded MCP App display stuck at 'Waiting for data...' — Autovisualiser and Apps extensions fail to render
signals.summary: The embedded MCP app display pane shows indefinite 'Waiting for data...' loading state. Visualization (donut, chart, sankey, etc.) and app extension outputs never render in the embedded pane. The same content renders correctly in a new window. Regression across multiple recent versions.
aliases: Autovisualiser stuck on Waiting for data
MCP App display iframe not receiving tool results
MCP apps embedded display never renders
signals.review_reason: Key feature regression: built-in Autovisualiser and Apps extensions are core product features, but their inline/embedded display is completely broken. Users must open content in a new window as a workaround. This is a regression affecting main product features across two consecutive versions (v1.34.0 and v1.34.1). Count=2 from distinct issue reports spanning v1.34.0 and v1.34.1.

source_issues.title: Embedded MCP App Display Not Rendering - Waiting for data... Stuck State
source_issues.evidence: Post-upgrade (v1.34.1), embedded MCP app display stuck on 'Waiting for data...' indefinitely. Regression: same content renders in new window. Affects Autovisualiser and Apps extensions. Multiple models (Minimax, Claude 4.5 haiku, 4.6 sonnet) all reproduce.

source_issues.title: The built-in Autovisualiser extension renders an empty placeholder showing 'Waiting for data...'
source_issues.evidence: All 8 autovisualiser tools stuck on 'Waiting for data...' in embedded iframe. MCP tool calls succeed but host does not post tool-result postMessage to iframe. Regression in desktop app's MCP App host bridge. Reproduces 100% on first use after fresh restart.

signals.topic: Thinking context not preserved for OpenAI-compatible providers — multi-turn tool conversations fail silently or with 400 errors
signals.summary: preserve_thinking_context flag is ineffective for OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenRouter, lmstudio, ollama, DeepSeek direct, etc.). Thinking content is stripped before being sent to the provider, causing DeepSeek reasoning mode to throw 400 'reasoning_content must be passed back' errors on the first tool-result turn. OpenRouter silently loses reasoning context.
aliases: reasoning_content must be passed back to API error
signals.review_reason: Provider compatibility breaking: reasoning-enabled DeepSeek (a popular cost-effective model) is completely broken for any tool-using conversation. OpenRouter users silently lose reasoning context. Both are popular provider configurations with no acceptable workaround.

source_issues.title: preserve_thinking_context ineffective for OpenAI-compatible providers
source_issues.evidence: agent_visible_content() strips Thinking content before reaching provider's format module. Fix identified: change filter_for_audience() in message.rs to preserve Thinking for Role::Assistant. Affects all OpenAI-compatible providers.

source_issues.title: deepseek-v4-pro (thinking mode): multi-turn tool calls fail with 400 reasoning_content must be passed back to the API
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek v4-pro with reasoning:true fails with HTTP 400 on first tool-result turn. Root cause: Goose strips reasoning_content from assistant messages when constructing next API request. No workaround — user must disable reasoning mode or stop using tool calls.

signals.topic: Windows: browser-based OAuth and authentication silently fails — blocks Copilot, Azure, GitHub login
signals.summary: On Windows (especially corporate environments), Goose fails to launch a browser for authentication flows (GitHub Copilot, Azure login, OAuth MCP servers). The UI says 'a browser window will open' but nothing happens. Root cause: executables (browser, az CLI) are not found in the restricted Windows PATH. Additionally, MCP OAuth opens 3 login pages in parallel on Windows 11.
aliases: MCP OAuth opens 3 login pages on Windows
signals.review_reason: Windows authentication broken: two distinct Windows-specific OAuth/browser auth bugs. Issue #9184 silently blocks all browser-based auth with no error shown. Issue #9181 opens 3 OAuth pages making auth impossible. Together they make Goose unusable with OAuth-based providers (GitHub Copilot, Azure) on Windows — a major platform.

source_issues.title: Windows: Browser not launching for authentication
source_issues.evidence: Browser launch silently fails on Windows corporate environments. No browser window opens despite UI promise. Blocks GitHub Copilot, Azure, and any browser-based OAuth. Root cause: executable path resolution fails for Edge/az in restricted Windows PATH. No error surfaced to user.

source_issues.title: MCP HTTP Server - Goose opens 3 OAuth login pages on Windows
source_issues.evidence: MCP OAuth flow opens 3 browser windows with 3 different client_id values on Windows 11. Regression from v1.27.2 to v1.28.0+. Only occurs on Windows. Each redirect uses different localhost ports (123, 124, 124). Logs show 3 auth flows starting in parallel.

signals.topic: Linux binary runtime dependency regressions: Vulkan loader and GLIBC 2.38 requirements break existing workflows
signals.summary: v1.34.0 introduces two Linux runtime dependency regressions: (1) libvulkan.so.1 required at startup even for cloud-only users who never use local inference, causing silent startup failure; (2) GLIBC 2.38 required, breaking Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Debian 12, and RHEL 8/9. Upgrading from v1.33.x silently breaks previously working installations.
aliases: v1.34.0 breaks on older Linux distributions
signals.review_reason: Release regression breaking existing users: upgrading from v1.33.x to v1.34.0 silently breaks Goose on multiple widely-used Linux distributions (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Debian 12, RHEL 8/9) with no documented breaking changes. Additionally, a Vulkan runtime dependency was silently added for cloud-only users who have no use for it. Both are clear regression defects introduced in v1.34.0.

source_issues.title: v1.34.0 published Linux binary requires libvulkan.so.1 at startup
source_issues.evidence: Linux tarball fails to start on systems without Vulkan loader. Binary links libvulkan.so.1 statically but dynamic linker rejects it before main() runs. Affects cloud-only users who never use local inference. Release notes had no Breaking Changes section.

source_issues.title: v1.34.0 requires libc6 2.38
source_issues.evidence: Goose v1.34.0 does not start on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (libc6 2.35). Error: GLIBC_2.38 not found. Regression: v1.33.1 works fine. Also affects Debian 12 and RHEL 8/9. Fix: downgrade to v1.33.1. PR #9075 moved build to Ubuntu 24.04 runners.

signals.topic: Telegram gateway: multi-step automation blocked by hardcoded 5-turn session limit

aliases: Telegram session turn limit not configurable
signals.review_reason: Main-flow block: Telegram gateway sessions are completely blocked after 5 tool calls regardless of user configuration. No workaround exists. Multi-step automation (login flows, data pipelines) is impossible, directly defeating the product's core value proposition for the Telegram integration channel.

source_issues.title: Telegram gateway: GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS hardcoded to 5

signals.review_reason: 明确的DoS场景：moderation模型不可用时所有技能写入被永久阻塞，代码中except块直接返回ScanResult('block')。影响所有技能开发工作流，属于关键功能不可用（skill evolution功能完全丧失）。提供具体代码行号和修复建议。

source_issues.title: Security scanner fail-closed blocks all skills when moderation model unavailable
source_issues.evidence: 代码证据显示：scan_skill_content()中moderation模型调用失败后，所有可执行和非可执行技能内容均被block返回。DoS场景明确：moderation模型不可用时所有技能写入被永久阻断，无法开发新技能或更新现有技能，工作流完全中断。

signals.topic: RunManager持久化未持有锁，存在进程重启后数据丢失风险
signals.summary: RunManager.create()在内存状态更新后才异步写入持久化存储，锁在持久化调用前已释放，若持久化失败则内存与持久化状态不一致
aliases: run manager data loss on restart
signals.review_reason: 数据持久化竞态条件明确：内存状态和持久化存储之间存在窗口期。若持久化失败（如磁盘满、数据库锁），已创建的run记录在进程重启后丢失，影响run历史完整性和可追溯性。属于明显成本/数据损失风险。

source_issues.title: Lock not held during RunManager store persistence
source_issues.evidence: 代码证据：async with self._lock: self._runs[run_id]=record; await self._persist_to_store(record) 锁在persist调用后才释放，但persist为async操作在锁外执行。若persist失败，内存已记录但持久化未完成，进程重启后run记录丢失。

signals.topic: 升级安装后checkpoint存储无限增长无管控，最高可达124GB
signals.summary: 遗留checkpointer配置与新的database配置共存时，checkpoint写入旧SQLite文件，导致存储无限增长且无清理机制
signals.review_reason: 真实磁盘压力事件：checkpoint存储增长至124GB，两个thread占大部分空间（状态载荷放大）。用户明确说明无启动警告、无迁移路径、无清理机制，导致磁盘空间危机。属于成本损失（存储费用）和服务可用性（磁盘满）双重影响。

source_issues.title: [runtime] Checkpoint storage can still grow unbounded after ThreadMeta search split
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供真实观察数据：升级后legacy checkpointer配置仍优先，checkpoint SQLite DB增长至约124GB，仅含数十个thread ID。明确disk-pressure incident场景，且无清理路径、无告警机制。

signals.topic: CLI config command ignores --config option and does not persist settings changes
signals.summary: In Cline CLI 3.0.7, the `cline config` command ignores the `--config` option entirely (always reads/writes global config), and any settings changes made in the TUI are not persisted to disk after exit. Users lose all configuration on every session.
aliases: global-settings.json not created after config changes
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports (count=2) both from the same user demonstrating that the core CLI config workflow is completely broken: settings are not persisted and the --config option is ignored. This blocks any non-default configuration use case and is explicitly contrary to documented behavior.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 config command ignores --config option
source_issues.evidence: Using `cline config --config test_config` produces the same global config output. The specified config directory is not used at all. Workflows defined in the target config are not visible.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 config does not persist configuration changes
source_issues.evidence: Changing values in `cline config` TUI appears to work in the current session but changes are lost on exit. No `~/.cline/data/settings/global-settings.json` file is created. Reproducible on every run.

signals.topic: CLI leaks processes and cannot resume sessions in --json mode
signals.summary: Cline CLI 3.0.7 leaks child `cline.exe` processes after task completion (processes accumulate indefinitely, consuming memory). Separately, combining `--json` with `--id` for session resumption always fails with a validation error, preventing scripted continuation of conversations.
aliases: cline.exe processes accumulate after task completion
JSON mode session resumption broken with --id flag
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but both critical CLI operational failures: (1) process leak causes unbounded resource consumption over time — a long-running server or automation setup will eventually exhaust memory; (2) session resumption in --json mode is completely broken, blocking programmatic/automation use of the CLI. Both affect the core non-interactive CLI contract.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 leaks running processes after handling a session task
source_issues.evidence: After completing even a simple task (`2+2`), a `cline.exe` process (245MB+) remains running and never terminates. Multiple invocations accumulate processes. Verified via tasklist and System Informer showing orphaned node processes.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 --json mode can't resume an existing session ID
source_issues.evidence: Using `cline --json --id <session_id> "prompt"` always returns error 'JSON output mode requires a prompt argument or piped stdin'. The session directory exists on disk but Cline fails to resume it. Reproducible on every call.

signals.topic: Grok models (grok-4, grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, grok-code-fast-1) enter infinite loop in Act/Plan mode
signals.summary: When using xAI Grok models with Cline in Act or Plan mode, the model repeatedly outputs the same 'Thinking' reasoning block without executing any tool calls, effectively freezing the task indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: Even at count=1, this is a primary-use-case blocker: Grok is a first-class supported provider, and all variants of the latest Grok models are unusable in Cline's core Act/Plan modes. The task never completes and the user has no workaround without switching providers entirely.

source_issues.title: Unable to select latest Grok Model. Stuck in infinite loop
source_issues.evidence: Multiple Grok models (grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, grok-code-fast-1, grok-4) all exhibit identical infinite loop behavior on trivial tasks like 'print hello world'. Model is trapped in a reasoning loop and never triggers tool execution. Confirmed on both Windows and Linux. Possibly related to xAI API migration (May 15 retirement of old endpoints).

signals.topic: Cline CLI ignores .clinerules from ~/Documents/Cline/ — inconsistent with JetBrains plugin
signals.summary: The Cline CLI does not read global rules stored in ~/Documents/Cline/ (the standard location used by the JetBrains plugin and documented for the VS Code extension). Users who configure rules in one IDE cannot use them when switching to the CLI, creating an inconsistent cross-platform experience.
aliases: rules inconsistency between CLI and IDE plugins
signals.review_reason: Cross-platform rule inconsistency means users cannot rely on a single rules configuration across IDE and CLI workflows. This is a meaningful experience degradation for users who switch between environments. Count=1 but clearly reproducible and documented with expected vs. actual behavior.

source_issues.title: Cline cli not take rules in windows from documents "~/Documents/Cline/"
source_issues.evidence: User configured global rules in JetBrains IDE plugin, verified they are saved in ~/Documents/Cline/, but the CLI does not pick them up. The CLI and JetBrains plugin use different rule paths, breaking cross-platform rule consistency.

signals.topic: Cline disregards user rejection of command and re-executes without asking for approval again
signals.summary: When Cline prompts the user to approve or reject a command and the user clicks 'Reject', Cline ignores the rejection and re-executes the same command without requesting approval a second time, bypassing the user's security decision.
aliases: Reject button does not prevent command execution
signals.review_reason: A security-critical approval bypass: Cline's core security mechanism (user approval before executing commands) is circumvented when a user explicitly rejects. This is not a feature request — it is a documented bypass of a safety control. Even at count=1, the severity and security implications justify inclusion.

source_issues.title: Cline disregards required approval
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly clicked 'Reject' on a command approval dialog. Cline re-ran the exact same command without prompting again, completely bypassing the user's rejection. The user's security intent was circumvented. Accompanied by a screenshot showing the Reject button being clicked.

signals.topic: Authentication / login failures block user access and onboarding
signals.summary: 用户在使用 Continue 时遇到多种认证失败场景：首次账户设置后登录失败、本地 LLM (LocalAI) 连接认证无法检测、请求头缺失导致认证错误。这些认证问题直接阻断用户进入主流程，导致核心功能完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 3 条独立 issue 覆盖不同认证失败场景（登录阻断、Header 认证、LocalAI 响应检测），均属主流程阻断，直接导致用户无法使用核心功能。count=3 满足高频阈值，且有明确用户影响证据（阻断登录、提供日志）。

source_issues.title: Login failed with "Not authenticated (user missing)" after account setup

source_issues.title: Responses from LLM's running from LocalAI are not detected

signals.review_reason: 3 条 issue 涉及文件读取的多个环节失败：token 硬限制阻断 Plan 模式、未知读取错误、大文件截断影响自动补全质量，均为用户主流程直接阻断，证据充分。

signals.summary: 自动补全功能在多个 IDE 平台（VS Code 和 JetBrains）均无法正常工作，用户多次报告补全结果为空或严重错误（截断/错误前后缀），导致 IDE 集成核心功能不可用。
signals.review_reason: 自动补全在 VS Code 和 JetBrains 两个主要 IDE 上均无法正常工作，虽 count=2 但涉及多个平台和不同补全失败模式，用户体验显著下降，核心 IDE 功能不可用，标记 P1。

signals.review_reason: count=1 但 review_reason 提供强证据：用户已定位根因（会话未重建）、有明确复现步骤、属于 MCP 核心协议处理缺陷，通信失败直接阻断使用 MCP 工具的主流程，故标记 P0。

source_issues.title: (sse) mcp restarts breaks communication
source_issues.evidence: MCP SSE 服务器重启后 Continue 无法重新建立会话，持续使用已失效的旧 session，用户已定位到根因并提供复现步骤

signals.topic: Context window not reset causing 400 errors with local LLMs
signals.summary: 本地 LLM (llama-server) 使用时，上下文窗口在对话之间不会重置，导致后续请求报错 '400 request exceeds available context size'，直接阻断本地模型使用流程。
signals.review_reason: 上下文窗口不重置是明确的技术缺陷，直接导致 400 错误阻断本地 LLM 主流程，虽 count=1 但用户影响证据明确（阻断请求、提供错误信息），标记 P1。

source_issues.evidence: 用户使用本地 llama-server，每次对话后上下文窗口不重置，导致 400 错误阻断后续请求，阻断本地 LLM 主流程

signals.topic: Tool re-execution on task retry causes duplicate side effects (payments, emails, trades)
signals.summary: When a CrewAI task fails and retries, any @tool decorated function that already executed fires again with no idempotency guard. This causes duplicate payments, emails, or trade executions — a critical issue for production workloads.
aliases: idempotency guard missing on tool retry
duplicate tool calls on task retry
no deduplication of tool calls across retries
signals.review_reason: This is a real production failure mode where tool re-execution on retry causes duplicate side effects. User provides a concrete code example (payment tool) and explicitly warns of financial/emails/trade impact. Count=1 because only one issue in the dataset, but the severity is high and well-evidenced with 28 community comments and a cross-reference to the same pattern in LangGraph. Not P0 because count=1 and lacks multiple independent reports in this dataset.

source_issues.title: Tool re-execution on task retry has no idempotency guard — duplicate payments, emails, trades possible
source_issues.evidence: User reports that @tool decorated functions execute twice on retry via max_retry_limit, exception handling, or external re-trigger. Example shows a payment tool firing twice causing duplicate charges. References LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 for the same failure pattern. 28 comments confirming the issue.

signals.topic: response_model / output_pydantic causes tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs (vLLM, LiteLLM, OpenAI-compatible)
signals.summary: Since v1.9.0, Task.output_pydantic is passed as response_model into the agent tool-calling loop on every iteration. For vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible servers, this causes the LLM to skip tool calls entirely and return structured JSON directly — tools never execute. Regression from pre-v1.9.0 behavior.
aliases: tools skipped when output_pydantic is set on non-OpenAI LLMs
vLLM tool calling broken with response_model
output_pydantic regression blocks tool execution on vLLM/LiteLLM
signals.review_reason: This bug completely blocks tool execution for any user running CrewAI with non-OpenAI LLMs (vLLM, LiteLLM, OpenAI-compatible) when output_pydantic is set. The user provides deep code-level analysis with line references, a minimal reproduction case, curl proof showing vLLM skips tools when response_format is present, and notes that CrewAI already has a provider-specific workaround for Gemini acknowledging this conflict. Well-evidenced with recent activity. Not P0 because count=1 in this dataset.

source_issues.title: [BUG] output_pydantic / response_model leaks into agent tool-calling loop, causing tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
source_issues.evidence: User provides detailed code-level analysis: response_model is passed on every iteration of the tool-calling loop. vLLM skips tool calls when both tools and response_format are present. LiteLLM routes to InternalInstructor bypassing tools entirely. Includes minimal reproduction with AddTool that never fires. 7 comments, recently active, clearly blocks any agent using non-OpenAI LLM with output_pydantic.

signals.topic: OpenAI API key works locally but fails with 401 invalid_api_key inside CrewAI Studio subprocess
signals.summary: Users report that a valid OpenAI API key works correctly outside CrewAI (via Python client and curl) but fails with 401 AuthenticationError when the same key is used inside CrewAI via crew.kickoff(). The VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch warning suggests environment variable propagation failure in subprocess execution.
aliases: OPENAI_API_KEY not propagated to CrewAI subprocess
API key fails inside crew execution but works outside
VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch causes API key to not reach CrewAI runtime
signals.review_reason: This issue blocks the primary execution flow (crew.kickoff()) with a 401 error even when the API key is confirmed valid outside CrewAI. The VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch evidence strongly points to an environment variable propagation bug in CrewAI's subprocess execution model. Full traceback provided showing the exact failure path. Not P0 because count=1 in this dataset.

source_issues.title: [BUG] OpenAI API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI with 401 invalid_api_key
source_issues.evidence: User provides full traceback showing AuthenticationError from openai SDK inside CrewAI subprocess execution. Same key tested with direct Python client and curl — works. VIRTUAL_ENV=/data/internal/venv mismatch with /shared_venv suggests subprocess environment isolation breaks API key propagation. Error repeats across multiple retry attempts in the traceback.

signals.topic: Dependency conflict between crewai opentelemetry packages and openlit blocks installation
signals.summary: crewai 1.14.4 locks opentelemetry-sdk to 1.35.0 but openlit 1.41.2 requires opentelemetry-sdk >=1.38.0, causing a poetry/pip dependency conflict that prevents simultaneous installation of both packages.
aliases: poetry lock fails due to opentelemetry version mismatch
signals.review_reason: Dependency conflict blocks installation/setup, which is a startup blocker but only affects users who need both crewai and openlit simultaneously. Proposed solution (relaxing opentelemetry version bounds) is straightforward. Lower priority than the runtime bugs above since it's a setup-time issue and count=1.

source_issues.title: [BUG] dependency conflict with OpenLIT
source_issues.evidence: User reports dependency conflict error when running 'poetry lock' with crewai 1.14.4, crewai-tools 1.14.4, and openlit 1.42.0. The conflict is at the opentelemetry-sdk level (1.35.0 vs >=1.38.0). Provides specific pyproject.toml configuration to reproduce.

signals.topic: Windows sandbox not supported — AI Agent automation workflows blocked for Windows users
signals.summary: Windows users receive 'sandboxing is not supported on Windows' error, causing AI Agent automation workflows to completely fail. This regression has persisted for approximately two months with no clear communication from the team, leaving Windows users without a working solution.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Windows 用户无法运行 AI Agent 自动化工作流，持续约两个月无解决方案。虽然仅单条 issue，但问题持续时间长、影响面广（所有 Windows 用户）、且无任何官方说明，属于明确的用户痛点而非功能缺失。

source_issues.title: Windows Bug : Windows users need a clear answer on the sandbox issue
source_issues.evidence: CLI throws 'failed to set up sandbox: sandboxing is not supported on Windows', causing AI Agent automation workflows to not work. User reports this has been ongoing for ~2 months with no team communication.

signals.topic: Headless mode (-p) 429 retry noise — automated pipelines cannot distinguish transient errors from permanent failures
signals.summary: In headless/non-interactive mode (-p), 429 rate limit responses produce excessive noisy retry output that pollutes stdout/stderr. Supervisor processes reading the output cannot programmatically distinguish a transient 429 (will resolve) from a permanent error (should abort), leading to incorrect failure detection or lost error messages.
aliases: non-interactive mode rate limit output pollution
signals.review_reason: 工作流阻断：headless/自动化场景下，429 重试输出无法让 supervisor 进程区分暂时性限流和永久性失败，导致自动化管道误判或丢失真实错误信息。这是核心自动化场景的体验降级，有明确用户影响证据（CI/agent pipeline 不可用）。

source_issues.title: Headless mode (-p): 429 retry output is excessively noisy and indistinguishable from permanent failures
source_issues.evidence: Supervisor processes reading stdout cannot tell if 429 is transient or permanent. Retry noise buries actual useful output in automated agent pipelines. User's CI/agent harness cannot determine whether session failed or succeeded.

signals.topic: 429 routing loop causes runaway token consumption and exhausts billing caps — financial loss
signals.summary: When hitting server-side 429 capacity limits, the NumericalClassifierStrategy enters an invisible infinite background exponential-backoff loop. Each retry recompiles and bundles the full Home Assistant schema into context, burning through millions of tokens in minutes and hitting billing caps, while the UI remains frozen on 'Thinking...'.
aliases: runaway 429 retry loop billing cap exhaustion
signals.review_reason: 计费异常/主流程阻断：429 无限重试循环导致用户在几分钟内消耗数百万 token 并触发计费上限，同时 UI 冻结无法交互。这是明确的财务损失问题，对付费用户造成直接经济损失，属于高优先级主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: BUG: Client-side 429 routing loop causes runaway token consumption and exhausts billing caps
source_issues.evidence: User burned through millions of tokens on Google Account and API within minutes due to invisible infinite retry loop. UI frozen on 'Thinking...' while retries consume massive tokens. User explicitly states: 'This is a real bad reputational issue when you're billing people for a fault in your own tools.'

signals.topic: Regression: session files lost and workspace files wiped/corrupted after Linux system reboot

Additionally, files in the targeted conversation directory are unexpectedly deleted or overwritten. This is a regression — behavior was correct in previous versions.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+数据丢失：会话持久化回归 bug，reboot 后会话完全丢失、工作区文件被删除或覆盖。用户明确指出是最新版本引入的回归问题，导致工作区状态无法保持，严重影响使用连续性。

source_issues.title: bug(cli): Regression in latest update causes complete session loss and folder wipes on system reboot
source_issues.evidence: Sessions created with /resume save disappear after reboot. Workspace files are corrupted or deleted. User explicitly identifies this as a regression introduced by the latest update.

source_issues.evidence: write_file tool truncates a 6,671-character character map and fails to close the object properly. Also corrupts large base64-encoded images. Agent itself acknowledges failure in session logs. Data integrity is compromised.
