signals.topic: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with ValueError when OCI container exec fails — agent run terminated
signals.summary: SandboxBackend.grep parses OCI runtime error messages as grep output lines, causing int() to raise ValueError on non-digit text after the first colon, which crashes the entire agent run loop. Three separate reports from different users confirm this is a real production crash with a clear minimal repro.
aliases: OCI runtime error parsed as grep output
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed user reports of a bug that causes agent runs to terminate abruptly. Root cause is well-understood (missing digit validation in grep output parser). Reproducible in production and test environments. Count=3 meets P0 frequency threshold.

source_issues.title: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with ValueError when container exec fails (parses OCI runtime error as grep output)
source_issues.evidence: Real prod crash: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ' exec failed'. OCI runtime error 'OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed: unable to start container process: chdir to cwd ("/workspace/references"): no such file or directory: unknown' is parsed as grep output because it contains colons, causing int(' exec failed') to crash. Entire tool node terminates agent loop.

source_issues.title: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with ValueError when container exec fails (parses OCI runtime error as grep output)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate filing with structured bug report template. Same root cause: int(parts[1]) on OCI error message containing ' exec failed'. Reproducible with Docker container work_dir that doesn't exist.

source_issues.title: `SandboxBackend.grep` crashes with `ValueError` when container exec fails
source_issues.evidence: Open bug with detailed minimal repro. Confirmed on deepagents==0.6.1. Explicitly states: 'Expected: GrepResult(error=..., matches=None); Actual: tool node crashes with ValueError, propagating out of the agent loop and terminating the run.'

signals.topic: deepagents-cli fails with OpenAI-compatible third-party endpoints due to incorrect API mode assumption
signals.summary: The CLI defaults to use_responses_api=true for all OpenAI providers, but third-party OpenAI-compatible services only support Chat Completions streaming. This causes 'No generations found in stream' errors, making the CLI unusable with providers like custom deepseek endpoints.
aliases: No generations found in stream on third-party OpenAI providers
signals.review_reason: User-impacting: CLI is completely broken for third-party OpenAI-compatible providers using Chat Completions streaming. Well-documented reproduction steps with config example. Despite count=1, the review_reason provides strong evidence: the entire CLI workflow is blocked for a common integration pattern (custom OpenAI-compatible gateways). No workaround without manual config.

source_issues.title: deepagents-cli fails on OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoints with 'No generations found in stream'
source_issues.evidence: User cannot use CLI with any OpenAI-compatible third-party provider that uses Chat Completions streaming (not Responses API). Detailed repro with base_url, model config, and error 'ValueError: No generations found in stream.' Suggested fix involves auto-detecting custom base URLs and defaulting use_responses_api to false. Workaround requires manual config override. 4 comments indicate ongoing discussion.

signals.topic: CompositeBackend.als() returns duplicated/wrong directory paths when queried path exactly matches a registered route
signals.summary: When als() is called with a path that exactly matches a registered route prefix, _remap_file_info_path incorrectly prepends the full route to already-absolute paths from the backend, causing path duplication (e.g., /memory/skills/memory/ instead of /memory/skills/test_skill/). This breaks SkillsMiddleware when loading skills.
aliases: SkillsMiddleware fails to load skills due to wrong path
signals.review_reason: Count=1 but user impact is clearly articulated: SkillsMiddleware (a core feature) fails to load skills when using CompositeBackend with StoreBackend routes. Minimal repro with expected vs actual output proves the bug. Confirmed reproducible on all platforms (pure logic bug). Review_reason explicitly names the blocked feature.

source_issues.title: `CompositeBackend.als()` returns wrong directory when path exactly matches a registered route
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly stated impact: 'This bug affects SkillsMiddleware when loading skills from StoreBackend via CompositeBackend routes, causing skills to fail to load or return wrong paths.' Minimal repro shows StoreBackend.als returns '/memory/skills/test_skill/' but CompositeBackend.als returns '/memory/skills/memory/' (wrong). Root cause traced to _remap_file_info_path duplicating path segments.

signals.topic: JavaScript eval interpreter tool does not await async IIFE return values — models receive unresolved Promises
signals.summary: The quickjs-based eval interpreter supports top-level await but fails to await Promises returned by async IIFEs when that IIFE is the final expression. Semantically identical code (top-level await vs async IIFE) produces different results: actual values vs Promise handles.
aliases: eval tool async IIFE Promise not awaited
JavaScript interpreter Promise handle instead of resolved value
signals.review_reason: Count=1 and single-repo, but the bug causes incorrect computation results (Promise handle vs resolved value) in a commonly-used tool. Models relying on the IIFE pattern get silently wrong outputs. The issue author explicitly notes models prefer IIFEs, making this a likely recurring failure pattern.

source_issues.title: Bug: `eval` interpreter tool does not await async IIFE return values
source_issues.evidence: Two minimal repro cases: (1) Top-level await works correctly, returns '123'. (2) Async IIFE with identical logic returns '<result kind="handle">[object]</result>' (unresolved Promise). Explicitly states 'many models lean towards IIFEs by default', meaning this is a common failure pattern, not edge case.

signals.topic: Headless/CI CLI runs hang indefinitely with no wall-clock timeout mechanism
signals.summary: deepagents-cli has --max-turns to bound roundtrips but no --timeout flag to enforce a wall-clock time limit. In headless and CI contexts, a hanging subprocess or slow model response causes the process to block forever, requiring external process management (SIGKILL, CI job timeout) with no clean exit.
aliases: no timeout flag for headless runs
CLI hangs indefinitely in CI environments
signals.review_reason: Count=1 and feature-request-adjacent (adds new flag), but the underlying issue is a real CI workflow failure: agent stalls cause indefinite hangs with no clean timeout. No workaround without external process management. Review_reason provides strong CI user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: `--timeout <seconds>` flag for headless runs
source_issues.evidence: Clear CI use case: 'In headless and CI contexts this matters: if the agent stalls mid-tool-call (e.g. waiting on a hanging subprocess or a slow model response), the process hangs indefinitely.' Proposed fix with asyncio.wait_for and exit code 124 (GNU timeout convention). Addresses a real CI/CI-equivalent workflow failure scenario.

signals.topic: langchain-openrouter 每次实例化泄漏 httpx socket pool，主流程资源耗尽
signals.summary: ChatOpenRouter 每次实例化都创建新的 httpx.Client/AsyncClient，HTTP 连接池不复用。在 LangGraph factory / FastAPI DI 等 per-request 实例化模式下，TLS socket 泄漏，连接数随实例数线性增长，在达到模型限速前先耗尽服务器资源，导致主流程阻断。
aliases: OpenRouter httpx default client not cached
signals.review_reason: 2个独立 issue 确认同一 bug：OpenRouter 每次实例化创建新 httpx.Client，per-request 模式（LangGraph/FastAPI）下 socket 连接线性泄漏，在达到模型限速前先耗尽服务器资源。明确的主流程阻断 + 资源耗尽场景，高置信度。

source_issues.title: langchain-openrouter: ChatOpenRouter creates fresh httpx clients per instantiation (no default-client caching)
source_issues.evidence: Socket count grows linearly with instance count. Pools embedded in discarded instances retain TLS connections until interpreter exit. Similar class of bug fixed for AzureChatOpenAI in #32489/PR #32531 but langchain-openrouter has same gap.

source_issues.title: langchain-openrouter: ChatOpenRouter creates fresh httpx clients per instantiation (no default-client caching)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #37498. Confirms socket leak confirmed after del + gc.collect() — httpx pools retain TLS connections until interpreter exit.

signals.topic: Ollama 多模态消息文本内容错误前缀 \n，vision 模型静默返回空响应
signals.summary: _convert_messages_to_ollama_messages 对多模态列表内容中每个文本段无条件加前缀 \n，导致 vision 模型因格式敏感而静默返回空响应，无任何错误或警告，极难调试。
aliases: Ollama multimodal text prefixed with newline
Ollama vision model silent empty response
signals.review_reason: Ollama 多模态场景下，文本内容被强制加 \n 前缀，vision 模型静默返回空响应，无任何错误提示，用户极难定位根因。生产环境关键功能静默失败，属明显用户体验下降，符合痛点定义。

source_issues.title: fix(ollama): multimodal message text content incorrectly prefixed with \n
source_issues.evidence: HumanMessage with list content (text + image) produces content starting with \n. Vision models sensitive to exact prompt formatting return empty responses silently. Confirmed case: deepseek-ocr requires single-line prompts and silently produces empty response. Failure is invisible with no error/warning and very hard to debug.

signals.topic: Chroma update_document() 要求 metadata 必填，与 add_documents() 行为不一致
signals.summary: add_documents() 允许不带 metadata 的 Document，但 update_document() 对同样结构抛出 ValueError，导致用户在更新向量时必须显式提供 metadata={}，行为不一致阻断常见使用模式。
aliases: Chroma update vs add metadata behavior
signals.review_reason: Chroma 向量库核心 API 行为不一致：add_documents 接受无 metadata 的 Document，但 update_document 拒绝同样结构。用户更新向量必须显式提供空 metadata，阻断常见工作流，属明显功能不可用/体验下降。

source_issues.title: Chroma.update_document() fails when Document metadata is omitted
source_issues.evidence: update_document() raises ValueError: Expected metadata to be a non-empty dict when Document omits metadata, while add_documents() accepts same structure. Users cannot update documents without explicitly supplying metadata={}, even when they don't need to modify it.

signals.topic: grep_search Windows 环境下 Python fallback 因编码问题静默跳过 UTF-8 文件
signals.summary: 在 ripgrep 不可用时，_python_search() 用 read_text() 无编码参数读取文件，Windows 默认编码 cp1252 导致有效 UTF-8 文件抛出 UnicodeDecodeError 并被静默跳过，搜索结果不完整。
signals.review_reason: grep_search 在 Windows 上遇 Python fallback 路径时，静默跳过有效 UTF-8 文件导致搜索结果缺失/不完整。用户感知到搜索结果与预期不符但无任何错误提示，属体验显著下降 + 关键功能不可靠。

source_issues.title: grep_search: Python fallback skips valid UTF-8 files on Windows due to read_text() encoding
source_issues.evidence: _python_search() calls file_path.read_text() with no encoding parameter. On Windows, default encoding is cp1252, causing valid UTF-8 files to raise UnicodeDecodeError and be silently skipped. grep_search results are incomplete or empty even though matching content exists in UTF-8 files.

signals.topic: ChatOpenAI with_structured_output + stream() 丢弃 response headers，调试关联丢失
signals.summary: 使用 with_structured_output(..., method="json_schema").stream() 时，响应头（x-request-id）未写入 response_metadata，导致用户无法将流式请求与提供商侧日志关联，生产调试困难。
signals.review_reason: ChatOpenAI 结构化输出 + 流式模式下响应头丢失，用户无法关联请求与提供商侧日志，生产环境调试受阻。虽非阻断主流程，但属关键可观测性缺失，P2 合理。

source_issues.title: ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output(..., method="json_schema").stream() drops response headers / x-request-id in response_metadata
source_issues.evidence: Streamed AIMessageChunk / final message objects do not contain HTTP response headers (x-request-id) in response_metadata when using with_structured_output + stream(). Same flow works correctly for non-structured streaming, AzureChatOpenAI structured streaming, and regular create(stream=True, include_response_headers=True).

signals.topic: interrupt() inside loops causes spurious extra resume iterations, corrupting agent state
signals.summary: When interrupt() is called inside a while loop within a node, resuming the graph causes extra iterations beyond what was intended, leading to state corruption and duplicate processing. The interrupt payload is surfaced but the loop re-executes unexpectedly.
signals.review_reason: interrupt() is a core LangGraph feature for human-in-the-loop workflows. When used inside a loop node, resuming the graph causes spurious extra iterations with stale interrupt payloads, directly corrupting agent state and producing wrong outputs. This is a main-flow blocking bug that affects any multi-step approval, form validation, or review workflow — LangGraph's primary differentiating use case.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Interrupt() in a loop will cause extra resumes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows that inside a while loop calling interrupt(), the first resume re-enters the loop and calls interrupt() again with the old payload, producing extra iterations. The loop logic checks `isinstance(answer, int) and answer > 0` but the re-entered interrupt() call uses stale state. This is a human-in-the-loop core feature bug that affects any form-validation or multi-step approval workflow built with interrupt().

signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization produces severe storage bloat (85%) and token overhead (37.8%) with no opt-out path
signals.summary: LangGraph's checkpoint serialization layer wraps every serialized value in extra metadata, producing 85% storage overhead and 37.8% token overhead in checkpoint payloads. Users of long-running agents or high-frequency checkpointing have no mechanism to opt out, leading to runaway storage costs and elevated LLM token consumption.
signals.review_reason: Storage bloat of 85% and token overhead of 37.8% with zero opt-out directly translate to quantifiable cost loss for any production deployment using checkpointing — LangGraph's core durability feature. The issue provides reproducible code, measured metrics, and a drop-in fix. Long-running or high-frequency workflows (e.g., per-turn checkpointing, multimodal agents) are disproportionately affected, making this a material production cost issue.

source_issues.title: LangGraph checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out path - reproducible with drop-in fix
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code demonstrates that a 4-turn ReAct state checkpoint is ~10MB in serialized form due to repeated metadata wrapping of every message and tool call. The issue includes a drop-in fix and quantifies the overhead: 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead per checkpoint. There is no opt-out mechanism. Downstream production users with long-running workflows and high checkpoint frequency will experience runaway storage costs and elevated API token usage from checkpoint serialization.

signals.topic: langgraph dev server cannot restart immediately after shutdown due to TIME-WAIT port conflict on port 2024
signals.summary: After running `langgraph dev` and stopping it with Ctrl+C, the port 2024 remains in TIME-WAIT state. Attempting to restart `langgraph dev` immediately fails with 'Port 2024 already in use', blocking the development workflow on every restart cycle.
aliases: langgraph dev port in use after restart
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core development loop of LangGraph — the `langgraph dev` command and its Studio integration. The conflict recurs on every single Ctrl+C restart cycle, making iterative development tedious or broken. Although count=1, the recurrence frequency (100% of restarts) and the fact that it affects the primary development workflow (langgraph dev + studio) make this a P0 workflow blocker with strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: `langgraph dev` falsely reports 'Port 2024 already in use' due to TIME-WAIT entries
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps: run langgraph dev, connect to studio or send a message, hit Ctrl+C to stop, try to restart immediately. Error: 'Port 2024 already in use'. The port is held in TIME-WAIT state by the OS after the server exits, not actually in use. This is a dev workflow blocker that occurs every single restart cycle, disrupting the iterative development loop.

signals.topic: Streaming agents expose malformed tool-call payloads as user-visible content when LLM emits stray tokens
signals.summary: When using graph.astream_events with tool-calling agents, the LLM occasionally emits stray tokens (commonly CJK characters) near tool-call boundaries. The provider's parser fails to classify the output as a structured tool call, and LangGraph relays the protocol-shaped text through on_chat_model_stream as ordinary assistant content, exposing internal function names and argument shapes to end users.
aliases: streaming tool call tokens leak to user
malformed streaming tool call payload exposure
stray tokens expose function names to users
signals.review_reason: Internal tool-call protocol data leaks to end users via the streaming API, exposing function names and argument structures. The actual tool call fails to execute because the malformed chunk bypasses on_tool_start/on_tool_end, causing the conversation to diverge from the intended agent flow. While intermittent, this is a production user-visible bug in a core streaming workflow, not just a theoretical issue.

source_issues.title: Streaming agents leak malformed tool-call payloads as user-visible content when the model emits stray tokens
source_issues.evidence: User reports in production that tool-call protocol fragments like 'to=functions.SomeTool 天天\n{"arg":"value"}' appear as ordinary assistant text to end users. Internal function names, argument shapes, and provider protocol details are exposed. The actual tool never executes because the payload was misclassified. The conversation diverges. Issue filed by a user on langgraph 1.0.1 in production, stating 'only happens every thousand chats or so but enough to be surfaced by users'.

signals.topic: SQLite checkpoint saver does not normalize channel values using new_versions, causing unchecked storage growth vs Postgres parity
signals.summary: The SQLite checkpoint saver stores full serialized checkpoints inline in the checkpoints.checkpoint BLOB, unlike the Postgres saver which normalizes channel values into a separate checkpoint_blobs table keyed by (thread_id, checkpoint_ns, channel, version) and writes only changed channels via new_versions. This divergence causes SQLite databases to grow much larger for long-running or multimodal workflows.
aliases: sqlite checkpoint storage bloat vs postgres
signals.review_reason: SQLite checkpoint storage diverges from Postgres in a way that causes material storage bloat (100+ GiB reported in production). While SQLite is positioned as a lightweight local saver, the absence of the channel/version normalization present in Postgres means stable large channel values are redundantly serialized on every checkpoint. This translates to direct storage cost for any local or edge deployment using SQLite checkpointing with substantial state.

source_issues.title: checkpoint-sqlite: storage model does not use `new_versions` to normalize channel values like Postgres saver
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code demonstrates that when only the 'small' channel changes, the SQLite saver still serializes the unchanged 'large' channel value (10MB) inline into both checkpoint rows. The Postgres saver uses new_versions to write only changed channels to checkpoint_blobs. A downstream LangGraph-based local workflow using SQLite checkpointing reported database growth above 100 GiB. Both checkpoint rows are 10MB each in the repro even though only 1 byte changed.

source_issues.title: unstructured api url is not configured for doc file processing
source_issues.evidence: User cannot process .doc files — unstructured API URL configuration missing. Both .doc and .docx file processing fail. Two separate users reported identical issue independently.

source_issues.title: unstructured api url is not configured for doc file processing

aliases: number variable type coercion float integer
ChatFlow conversation variable type changes between turns

aliases: custom metadata lost on memory update
signals.review_reason: Users lose important custom metadata (category, priority, source) that they explicitly stored during add(). This is silent data loss with no warning — metadata simply disappears after update(). Causes permanent loss of user-annotated data without any error or indication.

signals.topic: OpenAIEmbedder TypeScript SDK fails silently with OpenAI-compatible proxies due to base64 encoding default
signals.summary: TS SDK embedder defaults to encoding_format=base64 which OpenAI-compatible proxies (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama, OpenRouter) may not support. Results in silent failure with invalid 192-dimensional vectors instead of proper 768-dim embeddings.
aliases: TS SDK embeddings fail with LiteLLM/vLLM
signals.review_reason: Users using OpenAI-compatible proxy infrastructure (common for local/self-hosted embeddings) get silent failure where embeddings are corrupted. The vector store rejects the invalid vectors, causing recall search to fail. This blocks the main memory retrieval workflow with no actionable error message pointing to the embedder.

source_issues.title: Bug: OpenAIEmbedder in mem0-ts fails with OpenAI-compatible proxies (encoding_format default base64) — port #4058 to TS SDK

Results in silent failure with invalid 192-dimensional vectors instead of proper 768-dim embeddings. Users see 'Recall search failed: Bad Request' with no indication the embedder is at fault.

signals.topic: full raw conversation embedding causes token limit crash and poor deduplication recall
signals.summary: memory.add() embeds the full raw conversation as a single string for Phase 1 existing-memory search. Exceeding 8192 tokens causes 400 Bad Request crash before any memory is extracted. Even below the limit, multi-topic conversations produce blurred embeddings leading to poor recall.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is blocked for users with long conversations (common in production). The crash occurs before any memory extraction happens, so users lose the entire interaction. Even moderate-length multi-topic conversations produce degraded results as semantically unrelated content blurs the embedding.

source_issues.title: Raw conversation text embedded for existing-memory retrieval causes token limit crash and poor recall on multi-topic conversations
source_issues.evidence: memory.add() embeds the full raw conversation as a single string for Phase 1 existing-memory search. Exceeding 8192 tokens causes 400 Bad Request crash before any memory is extracted. Even below the limit, multi-topic conversations produce blurred embeddings leading to poor recall — semantically distant but relevant memories are missed entirely.

signals.topic: extraction pipeline produces mostly junk entries in production (97.8% junk rate documented)
signals.summary: Production audit across 32 days, 10,134 entries: 97.8% junk. Categories include boot file restating (52.7%), heartbeat/cron noise (11.5%), system architecture dumps (8.2%), hallucinated user profiles (5.2%), feedback loop amplification. After cleanup, recall quality improved immediately.
signals.review_reason: Fundamental reliability issue in production deployments. The extraction pipeline stores mostly noise (boot messages, system state, transient tasks, hallucinated facts) while users expect meaningful memories. This makes the system actively harmful — polluted vector stores degrade agent reasoning quality below baseline, as confirmed by Harvard D3 research. The Vim hallucination multiplied 808 times due to feedback loop.

source_issues.title: What we found after auditing 10,134 mem0 entries: 97.8% were junk
source_issues.evidence: Production audit across 32 days, 10,134 entries: 97.8% junk. Categories include boot file restating (52.7%), heartbeat/cron noise (11.5%), system architecture dumps (8.2%), hallucinated user profiles (5.2%), feedback loop amplification. Only 38 entries out of 10,134 were clean enough to keep. After cleanup, recall quality improved immediately. Harvard D3 research confirms 'indiscriminate memory storage performs worse than using no memory at all'.

signals.topic: graph memory poisoning enables attacker to influence agent recommendations through ordinary user input
signals.summary: Proof of concept demonstrates attacker message ('Alerzol is safe for Renovia syndrome') being stored as graph memory and later retrieved as trusted context to influence agent recommendation. In healthcare scenario, agent recommends harmful medication based on poisoned memory. No privileged access needed.
aliases: memory poisoning attack via user input
signals.review_reason: Demonstrated real-world harm scenario in healthcare where poisoned memory leads to incorrect medication recommendation. An ordinary user message can be stored as persistent graph evidence and later retrieved to influence agent behavior, including life-safety decisions. This is a high-severity integrity vulnerability affecting multi-agent shared-memory deployments.

source_issues.title: Responsible Disclosure: High-Severity Vulnerability in Shared Graph-Based Agent Memory
source_issues.evidence: Proof of concept demonstrates attacker message ('Alerzol is safe for Renovia syndrome') being stored as graph memory and later retrieved as trusted context to influence agent recommendation. In healthcare scenario, agent recommends harmful medication based on poisoned memory. No privileged access needed — attacker uses normal user interface.

signals.topic: FoundryEvals evaluate_agent() returns 400 BadRequestError for all agent evaluators when agent has tools
signals.summary: When using evaluate_agent() with default evaluators on an agent configured with tools, the Foundry evals service returns a 400 BadRequestError with MissingRequiredDataMapping. The framework only maps tool_definitions for evaluators in _TOOL_EVALUATORS but the service requires it for all evaluators that support it, completely blocking the evaluation workflow.
signals.review_reason: Critical evaluation workflow is completely blocked. Any user trying to evaluate an agent that uses tools (a very common pattern) gets a 400 error. Two separate reports confirm the same root cause. This is a main-flow failure for the FoundryEvals integration.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: FoundryEvals MissingRequiredDataMapping for tool_definitions on task_adherence and other agent evaluators
source_issues.evidence: 400 BadRequestError with MissingRequiredDataMapping thrown when evaluate_agent() is called on agent with tools. Root cause: _build_testing_criteria() only adds tool_definitions mapping for evaluators in _TOOL_EVALUATORS (5 explicit), but service requires it for all evaluators supporting it.

source_issues.title: Python: FoundryEvals: MissingRequiredDataMapping for tool_definitions on task_adherence (and other agent evaluators)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #5918. Same root cause confirmed.

signals.topic: Auto function calling strips null arguments, causing required-parameter function invocations to fail
signals.summary: When auto function calling is enabled, the model generates null values for optional parameters, but these nulls are stripped before invocation, causing 'Argument parsing failed' errors when the parameter is required. This is a main-flow blocking bug that prevents function-calling agents from working correctly.
aliases: null argument stripping in function calls
auto function calling argument parsing fails
signals.review_reason: Core function-calling workflow is blocked. The model correctly generates null for optional parameters but the framework strips them, causing required-param functions to fail at runtime. Has been confirmed reproduced by maintainers. This is a main-flow failure for auto function calling users.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Auto function calling removes null arguments
source_issues.evidence: Model generates {"location":"Seattle","unit":null} but null args are stripped, causing 'Argument parsing failed' error. Confirmed reproduced by maintainers. Required parameters fail to be passed when null is stripped.

signals.topic: Azure Functions hosting requires user-defined dummy OrchestrationTrigger to expose agent endpoint
signals.summary: When using Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.AzureFunctions, the agent endpoint fails to be exposed unless the user defines at least one [OrchestrationTrigger] function. Users must add a no-op dummy orchestrator just to satisfy the Functions runtime's discovery mechanism, indicating the source generator only scans the user's assembly for triggers.
aliases: Azure Functions agent hosting broken without dummy orchestrator
Functions source generator missing trigger detection
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking for .NET Azure Functions hosting users. The agent endpoint cannot be accessed unless a dummy orchestrator is added, which is a framework correctness issue. Users adopting the standard hosting pattern are blocked from deploying their agents.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Hosting.AzureFunctions requires a user-defined dummy [OrchestrationTrigger] to start
source_issues.evidence: Agent endpoint not exposed without a user-defined [OrchestrationTrigger] in the Functions app. User must add no-op dummy orchestrator. Root cause: Functions worker source generator only scans user assembly for triggers.

signals.topic: GitHubCopilotAgent MCP HTTP tool results silently dropped and presented as opaque AIContent, causing models to fabricate timeout errors
signals.summary: When GitHubCopilotAgent runs against MCP HTTP tools, tool results are wrapped in opaque AIContent { RawRepresentation = ... } instead of FunctionResultContent. The LLM cannot interpret this and emits fabricated timeout errors like 'MCP error -32001: Request timed out'. OnPostToolUse hook only fires for structured failures, not successful tool returns, causing silent failures.
aliases: MCP tool results dropped in GitHubCopilotAgent
models fabricate timeout errors for successful MCP calls
signals.review_reason: Critical silent failure pattern in GitHubCopilotAgent MCP integration. Tool results succeed server-side but are presented to the LLM as opaque uninterpretable data, causing the model to hallucinate timeout errors and potentially alter downstream behavior. This is a silent data-integrity failure that degrades agent reliability.

source_issues.title: Python: .NET: [Bug]: GitHubCopilotAgent silently drops MCP tool result events — projected as opaque AIContent instead of FunctionResultContent, causing models to fabricate timeout errors
source_issues.evidence: MCP HTTP tool results wrapped in opaque AIContent instead of FunctionResultContent. LLM misinterprets as timeout and fabricates errors 'MCP error -32001: Request timed out'. OnPostToolUse hook only fires for structured failures, not successful tool returns.

signals.topic: OTLP HTTP exporter sends telemetry to bare base endpoint instead of signal-specific /v1/{signal} paths, breaking observability
signals.summary: When configuring OpenTelemetry export via OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT with HTTP protocol, traces/metrics/logs are sent to the bare base URL instead of the correct signal-specific paths (/v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs). The OTel SDK treats programmatically provided endpoint= as a full URL without auto-append, causing all telemetry to be lost in production environments.
signals.review_reason: Observability is completely broken for OTLP HTTP users. All traces, metrics, and logs are misrouted to the wrong endpoint, meaning users cannot monitor or debug their production agents. This is a significant experience degradation with cost implications (observability data loss in production).

source_issues.title: Python: OTLP HTTP exporter sends to bare base endpoint instead of /v1/{signal} path
source_issues.evidence: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT configured with HTTP protocol results in traces/metrics/logs being sent to bare base URL instead of /v1/{signal} paths. OTel SDK treats endpoint= as a full URL without auto-append. All telemetry is misrouted.

signals.topic: VSCode extension silently drops remaining tests after slow (>10s) API test completes
signals.summary: The Playwright Test for VSCode extension aborts the test session when an API test (using request fixture) exceeds ~15-17 seconds, dropping the test result and leaving all subsequent tests in a perpetual 'pending' state. The underlying Playwright CLI completes all tests successfully but the extension UI discards results. This blocks the primary IDE-based testing workflow for any suite containing slow API tests.
signals.review_reason: Primary IDE testing workflow is completely blocked for suites with slow API tests. The extension silently discards results and abandons remaining tests, making the VSCode extension unusable for any real-world API test suite. The user has clear reproduction steps and a workaround (CLI), confirming this is a main-flow failure.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: VSCode extension aborts run after a single slow (>10s) API test — subsequent tests never execute despite
source_issues.evidence: Extension runs first 57 fast tests successfully, then when a 17s API test starts the UI counter changes from 57/80 to 57/57. Test completes in CLI (ok 58) but result is dropped. Tests 59-80 remain in pending state forever. Workaround: use npx playwright test CLI which runs all 80 successfully.

signals.topic: MCP server fails to launch browser when PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is set to a read-only location (NixOS, read-only Docker)
signals.summary: When the MCP server starts, it writes temporary browser profile data under the registry directory (which resolves to PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH when set). On systems where this path is read-only (NixOS immutable store, read-only Docker mounts, shared filesystem caches), the MCP server fails with EACCES permission denied and cannot start any browser. This blocks the entire MCP-based AI agent workflow.
aliases: MCP browser launch fails read-only path
signals.review_reason: This blocks the MCP server — a key AI agent integration — on NixOS and any read-only container environment, which are increasingly common deployment targets. The MCP tool cannot start a browser at all, making the entire integration unusable. Clear root cause identified in code, confirmed with a reproducible repo.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: MCP createUserDataDir writes profile data to PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, fails when path is read-only
source_issues.evidence: Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '<PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH>/mcp-chrome-for-testing-<hash>'. Specifically impacts NixOS (immutable Nix store), read-only Docker mounts, and shared filesystem browser caches. The nixpkgs playwright-mcp wrapper is affected. Only workaround is PWMCP_PROFILES_DIR_FOR_TEST env var which is undocumented.

signals.topic: playwright install-deps --dry-run no longer generates executable install script (regression in 1.60.0)
signals.summary: In version 1.60.0, the install-deps --dry-run command output format was changed from executable shell commands to human-readable (but non-executable) text. CI/CD pipelines that relied on capturing this output and replaying it in a separate container/build stage are now broken. This is a confirmed regression from 1.59.1 that directly breaks established CI/CD workflows.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression from a stable release (1.59.1 → 1.60.0) that breaks an established CI/CD workflow. The user cannot generate install scripts for their containerized build pipeline without this feature, and no in-tool workaround exists. This is a direct workflow-blocking regression.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: install-deps --dry-run can no longer be used to generate install script
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression introduced in v1.60.0 (commit b25fbe4). Previously output was executable shell commands; now prints human-readable but non-executable text. User's CI pipeline relied on this to generate a separate playwright-build container stage. No workaround available within the tool.

signals.topic: playwright-cli open fails with EINVAL on macOS when session name (e.g. repo basename) exceeds ~17 characters
signals.summary: The CLI daemon embeds the user-supplied session name directly into the Unix socket filename without length validation. On macOS, the tmpdir path is ~49 chars and the socket path limit is 104 bytes, leaving only ~17 chars for the session name. Repository basenames commonly exceed this length, causing the daemon to fail with EINVAL when opening a persistent browser session. This blocks AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) that use the repo basename as a stable session identifier.
aliases: CLI daemon EINVAL macOS socket path length
long session name fails CLI open
playwright-cli unix socket path too long
signals.review_reason: Blocks the CLI-based AI agent workflow on macOS — the default platform for AI coding tools. Any agent using a repo basename longer than ~17 chars cannot use playwright-cli persistent sessions. Root cause is precisely identified in the codebase. The workaround uses an undocumented env var, making it inaccessible to most users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: playwright-cli open fails with EINVAL when session name is long on macOS due to unix socket path length
source_issues.evidence: Error: Daemon pid=X: listen EINVAL: invalid argument on socket path. Session name 'awesome-coding-agent-orchestrators' (34 chars) triggers the bug. macOS tmpdir (~49 chars) + socket path structure leaves only ~17 chars for session name. Repository basenames routinely exceed 17 chars. AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor) are directly affected since they use repo basename as session name. Workaround: set undocumented PLAYWRIGHT_SOCKETS_DIR to shorter prefix.

signals.topic: @playwright/mcp reports 'Browser chrome is not installed' when ffmpeg is the actually missing executable
signals.summary: When recordVideo is enabled in the MCP browser context and ffmpeg is not installed, the MCP tool throws a misleading error stating 'Browser chrome is not installed' with instructions to run install-browser chrome. The actual missing executable is ffmpeg, which has nothing to do with the Chrome browser binary. This misattribution prevents users from diagnosing the real issue and blocks the MCP video recording use case.
aliases: MCP ffmpeg missing misattributed to chrome
MCP video recording fails with wrong error message
signals.review_reason: Key MCP functionality (video recording via recordVideo) is completely blocked with a misleading error message that sends users down the wrong troubleshooting path. The error claims Chrome is not installed when it clearly is. This is not just a UX annoyance — it makes a legitimate feature unusable because users cannot identify the real problem without deep knowledge of the codebase.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: @playwright/mcp reports "Browser "chrome" is not installed" when ffmpeg is actually the missing executable
source_issues.evidence: Chrome is installed and resolves correctly. The error message falsely claims browser is not installed. Running 'npx playwright install ffmpeg' fixes the issue, confirming ffmpeg was the only missing executable. Root cause: browserFactory.ts substring-matches 'Executable doesn't exist' on launch errors and rethrows via throwBrowserIsNotInstalledError naming the browser channel. Docker minimal repro provided.

signals.topic: Handlebars template execution_settings block is fully ignored when any PromptExecutionSettings object is passed
signals.summary: Two related bugs: (1) Passing any PromptExecutionSettings object (even just a ServiceId) causes the entire execution_settings block in Handlebars templates to be ignored, ignoring max_tokens, temperature etc. (2) Kernel.Invoke does not call functions specified in the Handlebars YAML prompt template, even with properly registered plugins.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bugs in Handlebars template processing. (1) Template-level execution settings (max_tokens, temperature) are silently ignored when any PromptExecutionSettings is provided, making template-defined settings unreliable. (2) Kernel functions referenced in templates are not called, breaking the core function-calling use case with Handlebars templates.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Handlebars Template execution_settings Ignored When Passing PromptExecutionSettings with ServiceId
source_issues.evidence: Providing a PromptExecutionSettings object with only a ServiceId causes the entire execution_settings block from the template to be disregarded, rather than being merged with or selectively overridden.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Kernel.Invoke Function is not calling other functions specified in the prompt template
source_issues.evidence: Kernel.Invoke with a Handlebars YAML prompt template that calls {{TimePlugin.get_time}} does not invoke the function, returning a message saying it cannot find the current user time. Functions are registered via DI.

signals.topic: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync throws NOT NULL constraint violation on json column
signals.summary: SqliteVectorStore/UpsertAsync raises 'SQLite Error 19: NOT NULL constraint failed: json' because the connector serializes non-vector properties as null/empty, violating the NOT NULL schema constraint. Users cannot upsert records at all, completely blocking vector store write operations.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot perform any upsert operations on SqliteVectorStore collections at all. This completely blocks the core write path of the vector store. The connector serializes non-vector fields as null/empty JSON, violating the database schema constraint. Reproducible with standard POCO models.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: [SqliteVectorStore] NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json during UpsertAsync
source_issues.evidence: UpsertAsync throws 'SQLite Error 19: NOT NULL constraint failed: json' even with valid non-empty property values. Workaround of manual raw SQL succeeds, confirming the connector serialization path is broken.

signals.topic: JSON prompt config reasoning_effort deserialization throws NotSupportedException
signals.summary: When 'reasoning_effort' is set in JSON prompt config, it is deserialized as JsonElement instead of string or ChatReasoningEffortLevel. Downstream code throws System.NotSupportedException, preventing reasoning effort from being configured via JSON.
signals.review_reason: Users who configure reasoning_effort via JSON prompt config files get an unhandled NotSupportedException at runtime. This blocks the entire prompt invocation path when reasoning effort settings are loaded from config.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: JSON prompt config bug when setting reasoning_effort
source_issues.evidence: Setting 'reasoning_effort: low' in execution_settings.default of a JSON config causes System.NotSupportedException: 'The provided reasoning effort System.Text.Json.JsonElement is not supported.' GetEffortLevel needs to call .ToString() on JsonElement.

signals.topic: Qdrant IsKeyPropertyTypeValid method not implemented causing GetCollection to throw
signals.summary: After upgrading Qdrant connector from 1.65.0-preview to 1.71.0-preview, GetCollection throws an error about IsKeyPropertyTypeValid not being implemented. This is a regression that blocks Qdrant vector store usage after a standard upgrade.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression from 1.65.0-preview to 1.71.0-preview. Users who upgrade the Qdrant connector package can no longer use GetCollection, completely blocking Qdrant vector store operations. Standard upgrade path breaks existing code.

source_issues.title: .Net Bug: Method IsKeyPropertyTypeValid in type Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.Qdrant is not implemented in 1.71.0-preview
source_issues.evidence: Regression from 1.65.0-preview to 1.71.0-preview. Calling GetCollection raises an error about IsKeyPropertyTypeValid not being implemented from the QdrantModelBuilder class. Blocks all Qdrant vector store operations.

signals.topic: RedisJsonCollection persists unannotated POCO properties into Redis JSON payload
signals.summary: RedisJsonMapper serializes the entire POCO record including all public properties, then only removes the key property. Non-vector-store-model properties (e.g., NotAnnotated:null) are persisted into Redis JSON, causing data integrity issues and unexpected schema inflation.
signals.review_reason: Users' POCO properties not intended for the vector store are silently persisted into Redis, causing data pollution and schema inconsistency. The unit test TODO confirms this is unintended behavior, not a design choice. Users may retrieve unexpected fields or face schema inflation.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: .NET: RedisJsonCollection JSON upsert includes unannotated POCO properties
source_issues.evidence: Unit tests contain TODO: 'Fix issue where NotAnnotated is being included in the JSON.' Serialized payloads include unexpected fields like 'NotAnnotated:null'. Violates documented behavior that only vector-store model fields should be stored.

signals.topic: Mobile/Remote 连接状态管理失效：配对后无法重连或清除陈旧设备

signals.topic: Responses streaming with structured output raises confusing Pydantic JSON validation error on incomplete/truncated responses
signals.summary: When using Responses streaming with Pydantic text_format and the API emits incomplete status (e.g., due to max_output_tokens truncation), the SDK parses and raises a Pydantic JSON validation error (e.g., 'EOF while parsing an object') on the output_text.done event before the terminal incomplete status is surfaced. This masks the real upstream failure and prevents application code from cleanly handling status='incomplete'.
aliases: streaming structured output incomplete JSON error
Pydantic validation error on incomplete response
response.incomplete masked by JSON parse error
signals.review_reason: Streaming responses with structured output auto-parsing raise a Pydantic validation error before the SDK can surface the actual incomplete status. This is a primary-flow failure: the application crashes with a confusing JSON parse error instead of gracefully handling the truncated response, directly blocking the user's streaming workflow and making the real error source opaque.

source_issues.title: Responses streaming structured output parses incomplete JSON before terminal incomplete status
source_issues.evidence: SDK raises Pydantic JSON validation error (e.g., 'Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing an object') on response.output_text.done before caller code can handle the terminal response.incomplete event. Reproducer: client.responses.stream with text_format=SomePydanticModel and max_output_tokens=1 triggers the parse-then-incomplete race.

signals.topic: README "Nested params" example calls non-existent client.chat.responses API and mixes API surfaces

signals.review_reason: A non-runnable example in the primary README documentation directly blocks users' first-time experience and copy-paste workflow. signals.topic: Multiple skills ingest unsanitized third-party/external content into agent context, enabling indirect prompt injection attacks
signals.summary: Multiple ClawHub skills (sergical/sentry-observability, yogesharc/supalytics, samj12/betbud-prediction-market-creation, seanwyngaard/web-scraper-as-a-service, tomasz-tomczyk/reposit, tsiontesfayechromaway/tester, wd1993/algorithm-solver, steipete/gog) fetch external content (telemetry, analytics, tweets, web pages, community posts, GitHub issues, workspace data, problem statements) and feed it directly into the AI agent's context with no sanitization, data-only fencing, or operator confirmation. In each case the same agent holds sensitive mutation authority (chain transactions, shell access, file access, authenticated API calls, site management).
aliases: unsanitized third-party content in agent context
signals.review_reason: Eight independent security findings all share the same root cause: external/third-party content is fed directly into the agent context with no sanitization, data-only fencing, or operator confirmation, while the same agent holds sensitive mutation authority. The attack surface is real and documented per-skill with specific attacker-controllable fields and concrete mutation sinks (chain transactions, shell execution, authenticated API calls, file system access). Surface-level scanning passes these skills as legitimate, making them exploitable in practice.

signals.topic: WSL gateway validation fails due to hardcoded TFM path, may launch stale tray executable

signals.topic: WebSocket receive loop has no back-pressure; slow capabilities block health pings and concurrent invokes
signals.summary: WindowsNodeClient's sequential WebSocket receive loop awaits each capability execution inline. Long-running capabilities (screen recording, shell commands, STT transcription) block all other inbound messages on the same connection — including health pings, pair events, and cancellation requests. Results in gateway considering the node dead during long captures, and user-initiated cancellations being queued indefinitely.
aliases: Long-running node capabilities block WebSocket message loop
Head-of-line blocking in WebSocket receive loop
Health pings blocked during screen.record or long shell commands
signals.review_reason: Performance and availability issue: slow node capabilities (screen recording, shell commands, STT) block all concurrent WebSocket messages including health pings. This causes the gateway to incorrectly mark the node as dead during legitimate long-running operations, and prevents user cancellation requests from being processed. Observable user impact is session instability and inability to interrupt long operations.

source_issues.title: [deep-review] A10: WindowsNodeClient single-threaded receive loop has no back-pressure (head-of-line blocking)
source_issues.evidence: ProcessMessageAsync awaits capability execution inline on the receive loop. A slow screen.record, system.run, or stt.transcribe blocks every other inbound message including health pings and pair events. Gateway may decide node is dead and tear down the session. Cancellation requests queued indefinitely during long operations. Explicitly contrasted with MCP server's 16-concurrent semaphore that handles this correctly.

signals.topic: V1/V2 exec-wrapper shell detection diverged; non-standard shells bypass exec security policy
signals.summary: The V1 exec-wrapper detector (active in the live exec-approval path) does not recognize zsh, dash, ash, ksh, or fish shells. The V2 detector added these shells. An agent invoking zsh -c with a policy like 'Allow: bash, Deny: rm' will bypass the policy because neither rule matches the unrecognized shell. The default 'deny' saves the system, but legitimate operator policies become ineffective.
aliases: zsh/dash/ash/ksh/fish shell wrappers not recognized by exec gate
Security policy Allow/Deny rules bypassed by unrecognized shell types
signals.review_reason: Security policy bypass: exec-wrapper detectors diverged; zsh/dash/ash/ksh/fish shells are not recognized by the live V1 exec-approval gate. Operator-defined Allow/Deny policies (e.g., 'Allow: bash, Deny: rm') fail to match these shells, silently falling through to default-deny behavior. While default-deny is the safety net, this breaks legitimate operator security policies and creates inconsistent behavior across shell types.

source_issues.title: [deep-review][duplication] D3: V1 and V2 exec-wrapper detectors have diverged on shell vocabulary and flag handling
source_issues.evidence: V1 detector (live exec-approval path) does not recognize zsh/dash/ash/ksh/fish. V2 detector added these shells. Agent invoking 'zsh -c rm -rf' reaches the policy evaluator as a literal 'zsh -c rm -rf' string. Policy rules written for bash bypass silently. Default 'deny' is the safety net but custom Allow/Deny policies become ineffective for non-standard shells.

When handlers genuinely fault, the swallow makes diagnosis impossible; the reported symptom is 'activity stream randomly stops updating' with no log evidence.

Activity stream stops updating with no error logs

The user-visible symptom is 'activity stream randomly stops updating' with no log evidence to diagnose. This directly impairs user supportability and can represent data loss (e.g., event handlers silently failing to execute). Count=41 affected files demonstrates this is a systemic pattern, not an isolated incident.

signals.review_reason: System upgrade can corrupt a running gateway into a half-swapped state with missing modules, directly causing crash loops. This is a high-severity operational failure that can take down the entire gateway and block all traffic for all channels.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: system npm upgrade can leave running gateway in transient half-swapped package/plugin state
source_issues.evidence: During live Linux system-global upgrade from 2026.5.16-beta.3 to 2026.5.18, running gateway briefly loaded half-swapped package/plugin state and logged missing bundled modules including @openclaw/codex missing ./string-coerce-LndEvhRk.js.

signals.topic: Uncaught tree-sitter QueryError: invalid node type crashes repo-map generation on multi-language repos
signals.summary: Aider crashes with an uncaught tree_sitter.QueryError when generating the repo map for repositories containing certain language file structures. The error 'Invalid node type: module' is raised in repomap.py get_tags_raw(), blocking the repo-map feature.
aliases: tree-sitter query invalid node type crash
signals.review_reason: Two independent users (Linux and macOS) hit the same uncaught tree_sitter.QueryError in repomap.py, crashing the entire aider session when the repo-map feature is triggered. The crash occurs during the get_repo_map() flow, a core feature. count=2 with cross-platform evidence strengthens confidence. The feature is unusable for users with affected file structures.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module — raised in repomap.py get_tags_raw() called from get_tags() -> get_ranked_tags() during repo-map generation. Linux platform. Uncaught exception crashes the entire session.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: Identical tree_sitter.QueryError crash on macOS platform. Both users hit the same code path (repomap.py:302) when generating repo maps, indicating the tree-sitter query fails for certain language file structures across platforms.

signals.topic: Uncaught RuntimeError: symlink loop causes aider startup crash
signals.summary: When the working directory contains a symlink loop, aider crashes with an uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py resolve(), preventing the tool from starting entirely.
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash: the exception propagates uncaught through main() -> coder.run() -> send_message() -> format_chat_chunks() -> get_repo_messages() -> get_repo_map(), completely blocking the user's primary workflow. The user cannot use aider at all when this condition exists. Single-user evidence is strong because it demonstrates a complete tool unavailability scenario.

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 1239
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Symlink loop from '/home/steve/MEGA/ea/EA' — uncaught exception causes aider to crash immediately on startup, blocking the main workflow. User cannot use aider at all until the symlink is resolved or the path is excluded.

signals.topic: Uncaught NotImplementedError: non-relative glob patterns crash /read command on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows, using a glob pattern with the /read command causes an uncaught NotImplementedError in pathlib.py, crashing aider during command processing.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow runtime crash: a user attempts to use the /read command with a glob pattern, which raises NotImplementedError from pathlib.glob() and is not caught, crashing the command and interrupting the active session. While single-incident, the uncaught exception in a core interactive command warrants P1.

source_issues.title: Uncaught NotImplementedError in pathlib.py line 1090
source_issues.evidence: NotImplementedError: Non-relative patterns are unsupported — raised in pathlib.py glob() called from commands.py cmd_read_only(), crashing the /read command. The error occurs during command execution, breaking a core interactive workflow. Windows-specific but user-impacting.

signals.topic: Uncaught OSError: extremely long --system-prompt argument causes startup crash (errno 63)
signals.summary: When the system prompt exceeds filesystem path length limits, Path.is_dir() raises an uncaught OSError with errno 63 (File name too long), crashing aider before it can start.
aliases: OSError errno 63 file name too long
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash triggered by a legitimate use case (long system prompt). The OSError errno 63 propagates uncaught from pathlib.is_dir() during argument processing in main(), preventing aider from starting. The crash occurs before any user interaction, constituting a complete workflow blockage.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 1222
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long — raised when a very long --system-prompt value is passed and Path() operations treat it as a path. The crash occurs in main() before coder.run(), completely blocking startup. Users with verbose system prompts cannot use aider.

signals.topic: Silent flag mismatch: benchmark.py uses --read-model-settings while main CLI/docs use --model-settings-file, causing settings to not load with no error
signals.summary: The benchmark.py script's --read-model-settings flag does not match the main CLI's --model-settings-file flag documented in the adv-model-settings docs. Users following documentation links silently load no settings, causing benchmark to hang in long-decode loops for hours without error feedback.
aliases: benchmark flag name mismatch silent failure
model settings not loaded in benchmark
signals.review_reason: This is a significant UX/data loss issue: the user spent multiple hours debugging a silent failure where model settings are not applied to benchmark. The failure mode is particularly insidious — hours of hang time instead of fast error — and it was previously reported and never resolved. However, count=1 on a single user-reported scenario, with no evidence of broader impact, so P2 is appropriate. The silent nature (no error, no warning) means the user cannot detect the problem without deep understanding of the codebase.

source_issues.title: benchmark.py uses `--read-model-settings` but main cli + docs say `--model-settings-file`
source_issues.evidence: User spent 'a couple of hours' debugging a benchmark setup against a local vllm endpoint before discovering the flag name mismatch. Settings YAML silently fails to load — no error, no warning. Qwen-family AWQ models hang in long-decode loops without min_p/top_p settings from the YAML. The bench has LONG_TIMEOUT=24h, so the failure manifests as a silent multi-hour hang rather than a fast failure. Previously reported in #2766 (open since Jan 2025) and never resolved.

signals.topic: undici v7 upgrade breaks HTTP response decompression causing JSON parse errors on compressed endpoints
signals.summary: After upgrading to undici v7, the custom undici.Agent used for connection pooling no longer decompresses Brotli/gzip responses, causing all HTTP requests against compressed endpoints (especially OpenAI CDN) to fail with binary garbage / JSON parse errors. Every web-search-enabled eval and OpenAI API call is affected.
aliases: custom dispatcher fails to decompress responses
Brotli/gzip response parsing fails after undici upgrade
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断级别 bug：undici v7 升级后，自定义 Agent 的 decompress interceptor 被移除，导致所有使用连接池的 HTTP 请求对 gzip/br 压缩响应无法解码。用户在调用 OpenAI API（含 web-search evals）时看到 binary garbage JSON parse error，100% 的测试用例全部失败。此 bug 已在代码层面定位到 getOrCreateAgent 函数，影响范围覆盖所有 HTTP provider，属于发布后 regression。

source_issues.title: fetch() with custom undici Agent does not decompress Content-Encoding responses (Brotli/gzip → garbage)
source_issues.evidence: All HTTP providers hitting OpenAI CDN (web-search evals, responses API, chat completions) fail with 'Error parsing response: Unexpected token <binary>' because undici v7 custom Agent returns raw compressed bytes instead of decoded JSON. Symptom is binary garbage (Brotli stream, first byte 0x1B/0x0B/0x0F) in Received text field. Triggered by PR #7137 (undici v7 upgrade). Affects essentially every compressed HTTP call.

signals.topic: Homebrew 安装失败：@esbuild/darwin-arm64 可选依赖缺失导致 promptfoo 无法启动
signals.summary: macOS ARM64 用户通过 Homebrew 安装 promptfoo 后，运行任何命令（如 `promptfoo code-scans run`）时 esbuild 报错找不到 @esbuild/darwin-arm64 包，进程崩溃退出。这是 esbuild 的 optionalDependencies 在 Homebrew 安装时被跳过的典型问题。
aliases: brew install promptfoo esbuild darwin-arm64 not found
esbuild optional dependency missing on macOS ARM64
signals.review_reason: 启动崩溃级别 bug：macOS ARM64 用户通过 Homebrew 安装后，promptfoo 完全无法启动，报 esbuild 缺失 @esbuild/darwin-arm64 可选依赖错误。这是核心功能阻断，用户甚至无法运行基础命令（如 code-scans）。

source_issues.title: The package "@esbuild/darwin-arm64" could not be found
source_issues.evidence: 用户通过 Homebrew 安装 promptfoo 后，运行 promptfoo code-scans run 立即崩溃：Error [TransformError]: The package "@esbuild/darwin-arm64" could not be found, and is needed by esbuild. node_modules/esbuild/lib/main.js:2040. 这是典型 esbuild optionalDependencies 在非 npm 安装场景下未被正确拉取的问题，导致核心功能完全不可用。

signals.topic: rag-poisoning 红队插件生成的断言找不到对应的 grader 导致评测完全失败
signals.summary: 用户运行 redteam run 使用 rag-poisoning 插件时，promptfoo 成功生成测试用例，但评测阶段所有用例均以 'Invariant failed: Unknown grader: promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning' 错误中止。根本原因是 rag-poisoning 插件注册了但没有对应的 grader 存在于 graders.ts 中，导致 100% 的 redteam 扫描失败。
aliases: redteam plugin assertion unknown grader error
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：rag-poisoning 是 promptfoo 红队安全评测的核心插件之一，用户运行 redteam run 时该插件完全失效——测试生成成功但评测 100% 报错。这是红队扫描流程的阻塞性 bug，属于 plugin/grader 注册不一致导致的系统性问题。

source_issues.title: Bug: `rag-poisoning` tests fail during evaluation with `Unknown grader`
source_issues.evidence: rag-poisoning 插件被 createRemotePlugin 注册，但 src/redteam/graders.ts 中不存在对应的 promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning grader。运行 redteam run 后生成测试用例成功（2个测试），但评测阶段所有用例报 Unknown grader 错误，0 passed, 2 errors (100%)。用户被迫手动将断言替换为 llm-rubric 才能继续使用。

signals.topic: download_loader import removed from llama_index breaks haystack external integration
signals.summary: The `download_loader` API was removed from llama_index, causing ImportError in downstream integrations like haystack. This is a breaking change that blocks cross-framework usage.
signals.review_reason: This is a breaking API change that actively blocks external integrations. While labeled 'question', the issue provides a full ImportError traceback and demonstrates that the haystack-llamhub connector is non-functional due to removal of download_loader. This represents a release/packaging change with confirmed user-facing breakage.

source_issues.title: [Question]: download_loader cannot be imported from llama_index
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'download_loader' from 'llama_index' when integrating with haystack. Full traceback shows failure during test collection in haystack-llamhub connector.

signals.topic: SimpleChatEngine crashes with ValueError when ChatMessage contains multiple blocks during streaming
signals.summary: SimpleChatEngine crashes with ValueError when consuming streamed responses because awrite_response_to_history() tries to set .content on a ChatMessage that contains multiple blocks, which is not supported.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed application crash in the main chat engine workflow. The bug has a complete traceback, reproduction steps, and clear root cause: awrite_response_to_history() attempts to assign .content on a multi-block ChatMessage, which raises ValueError and blocks the entire streaming chat flow.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ValueError when ChatMessage contains multiple blocks in SimpleChatEngine
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: ChatMessage contains multiple blocks, use 'ChatMessage.blocks' instead. Crash occurs during astream_chat() when consuming streamed response and writing back to chat history. Full traceback shows crash in awrite_response_to_history at line 252 of types.py.

signals.topic: GoogleGenAIEmbedding returns single aggregated embedding instead of per-text embeddings with SDK v1.71.0+
signals.summary: When using google-genai SDK >=1.71.0, get_text_embedding_batch returns one aggregated embedding instead of one embedding per input text, breaking batch embedding in RAG pipelines.
aliases: embedding API breaking change with newer SDK
signals.review_reason: Core embedding functionality is broken for users on newer google-genai SDK. Batch embeddings are fundamental to RAG pipeline indexing — returning a single aggregated embedding instead of per-text embeddings corrupts the entire retrieval pipeline. Bug has explicit expected vs actual output and a proposed fix (wrap strings in Content objects).

source_issues.title: [Bug]: GoogleGenAIEmbedding with gemini-embedding-2 produces aggregated embeddings instead of individual ones with google-genai SDK v1.71.0+
source_issues.evidence: get_text_embedding_batch(["Hello", "Test", "Useful"], expected len=3, actual len=1. Root cause: newer google-genai SDK changed behavior when passing raw strings to contents parameter, now aggregates instead of treating each string separately.

signals.topic: google_genai returns misleading error message when uploading >20MB files with vertexai config
signals.summary: Uploading files >20MB via vertexai client produces a cryptic error message ('This method is only supported in the Gemini Developer client') instead of a clear file-size limit error.
aliases: vertexai large file upload error message
signals.review_reason: Error message quality issue that causes user confusion and delays troubleshooting. While the underlying limitation is from Google's SDK, llama-index could intercept and provide a clearer error message. Count=1 and the impact is non-blocking (user can work around once they understand), making this P2 rather than P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: google_genai produces cryptic errors for >20MB file uploads with vertexai config
source_issues.evidence: Confusing error message 'This method is only supported in the Gemini Developer client' when uploading >20MB files via vertexai, instead of a clear size limit error. Issue references upstream SDK limitation and proposes improved error handling within llama-index.

signals.topic: LlamaParse image download button non-functional in cloud UI
signals.summary: The image download button in LlamaParse cloud UI remains grey and non-clickable, preventing users from downloading parsed images even though they display correctly in previews.
aliases: LlamaParse cloud UI image extraction broken
signals.review_reason: Key feature of LlamaParse (image extraction/download) is completely non-functional in the cloud UI. While the issue was opened on the cloud product, llama_index is the upstream library and this functionality is core to the parsing pipeline. The bug has clear visual evidence (screenshots) and actively blocks the documented workflow of integrating parsed images into markdown files.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Download of images is not possible
source_issues.evidence: Download button in LlamaParse cloud UI remains grey and non-functional. Images display correctly in markdown and image previews but cannot be downloaded. Multiple screenshots provided. User is non-technical and cannot work around via code.

signals.topic: npm registry broken publish blocks install path — @ruvector/sona@0.1.6 empty tarball
signals.summary: @ruvector/sona@0.1.6 published as empty tarball (only README.md + package.json, no index.js, no native .node binaries), breaking @claude-flow/neural and all downstream packages
signals.review_reason: User-blocking installation failure: empty npm tarball causes @claude-flow/neural import to fail at runtime with 'Cannot find package .../index.js'. ~40K weekly downloads blocked for all fresh installs. Cascaded to all consumers (cli, claude-flow, ruflo). Explicit count evidence in issue body.

source_issues.title: [upstream] @ruvector/sona@0.1.6 is an empty publish — broke @claude-flow/neural until alpha.9 pinned around it
source_issues.evidence: Empty tarball: only README.md + package.json, no index.js or native .node binaries. ~40,000 weekly downloads of @claude-flow/neural were blocked between 0.1.6 publish and alpha.9 fix. Cascaded to @claude-flow/cli, claude-flow, ruflo.

signals.topic: CLI npm install fails with 'Invalid Version' — default install path broken
signals.summary: @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38 fails with npm 'Invalid Version' error due to transitive dep @huggingface/transformers@4.2.0 manifest having an empty version field, breaking npx default install
signals.review_reason: Primary install path failure: npx @claude-flow/cli@latest is completely broken for users. MCP server, doctor, and status tools are all unavailable on the default install path. This is a direct user-blocking issue, not a secondary workflow failure.

source_issues.title: @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38 fails with npm 'Invalid Version' (regression of #1147 pattern)
source_issues.evidence: npm install fails with 'Invalid Version:' (empty version string) in npm arborist dedupe step. Affects npx @claude-flow/cli@latest on npm 11.x / Node 24+. Root cause: transitive dep @huggingface/transformers@4.2.0 has empty version field in manifest. MCP server / doctor / status all unavailable on default install path.

signals.topic: pre-bash security hook silently bypasses dangerous-command validation — safety gate is a no-op
signals.summary: hook-handler.cjs reads wrong field for bash command input, causing .toLowerCase() on an object which throws silently. Dangerous commands like 'rm -rf /' pass through the safety gate without blocking, but exit 0 as if validated.
signals.review_reason: Security bypass with confirmed exploit: documented 'validate command safety' gate is silently a no-op. Verified reproduction showing 'rm -rf /' passes without blocking. Severity explicitly called out as medium because coverage list is narrow, but bypass is confirmed and real.

source_issues.title: pre-bash hook silently skips dangerous-command validation on real Claude Code payloads
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction confirmed: 'rm -rf / --no-preserve-root' sent via Claude Code PreToolUse schema passes hook validation and exits 0. Root cause: toolInput is an object {command: '...'}, not a string. .toLowerCase() on object throws TypeError, swallowed by 5s safety timer, exits 0 as [OK].

signals.topic: browser_session_record fails on missing -d/--dimension flag — entire 23-tool browser stack inert
signals.summary: ruflo-browser 0.2.0 MCP tool browser_session_record invokes ruvector rvf create without required --dimension flag, causing every call to fail before opening a session. All downstream browser skills (login, record, extract, form-fill, auth-flow, replay, screenshot-diff) are unreachable.
signals.review_reason: Full feature stack blocked: the entire 23-tool ruflo-browser package is inert because session creation (a prerequisite step) fails on every invocation. Not a minor degradation — it renders the entire plugin unusable.

source_issues.title: ruflo-browser 0.2.0: `browser_session_record` fails — `ruvector rvf create` missing required `-d, --dimension` flag
source_issues.evidence: Every browser_session_record call fails: 'error: required option -d, --dimension <n> not specified'. Blocks all 23 downstream tools in the browser stack: browser-login, browser-record, browser-test, browser-extract, browser-form-fill, browser-auth-flow, browser-replay, browser-screenshot-diff.

signals.topic: Subagent SendMessage/TaskUpdate unavailable in Claude Code harness — hive-mind coordination silently fails
signals.summary: Claude Code Agent subagents lack SendMessage and TaskUpdate tools in their tool allowlist, causing hive-mind coordination to silently fail. Subagents either abort with errors or work open-loop producing stale/inconsistent output. This contradicts the shipped 'SendMessage-First Coordination' pattern.
signals.review_reason: Real but non-blocking user impact: coordination failure leads to either agent aborts or silent data corruption (inconsistent outputs). Workaround exists (memory-as-bus pattern) but the shipped canonical pattern is non-functional for subagents. Downgraded from P0 because workaround is documented and it is a harness-level issue rather than a product bug per se.

source_issues.title: Subagents cannot use SendMessage/TaskUpdate in Claude Code harness — hive-mind coordination silently fails
source_issues.evidence: 7-agent swarm audit: 2 of 7 agents aborted with 'SendMessage is not present in this environment'. 5 others silently worked open-loop. hive-mind_broadcast reports 'Hive-mind not initialized' from subagent context. Either agents abort with errors (visible failure) or silently work open-loop producing stale/inconsistent output (invisible failure — much worse).

signals.topic: CDP执行上下文被DevTools重定向至隔离环境，导航和eval命令静默失败
signals.summary: 使用--cdp附加到已有Chromium时，若目标标签页同时打开了Chrome DevTools，Runtime.evaluate、Page.navigate等操作会被路由至与页面主世界完全断开连接的次级执行上下文。CLI报告成功并返回看似合理的结果，但用户可见的标签页不受影响，导致导航、快照、eval等核心命令静默失效。
aliases: CDP context targeting wrong execution context when DevTools is open
phantom context on --cdp attach with DevTools
secondary execution context when DevTools is open
signals.review_reason: 核心命令(open/navigate/eval/click)静默失效是主流程阻断级别的问题，症状严重且已有详尽重现步骤和根因分析。虽然count=1，但置信度极高。

source_issues.title: `--cdp` eval/open silently target a secondary execution context when Chromium DevTools is open on the same target
source_issues.evidence: agent-browser open报告成功但可见标签页未移动；eval返回与地址栏不同的location.href；doctor检查通过但无法发现该问题；已通过对比Python raw CDP调用确认根因。

signals.topic: 会话结束后遗留的Chrome Helper进程以高CPU持续运行，导致资源泄漏
signals.summary: agent-browser退出后，头less Chrome Helper子进程在临时profile路径下保持存活，单个进程CPU占用可达85-100%，累计消耗5-6个CPU核心，需手动kill。影响机器续航和性能。
aliases: orphaned Chrome Helper processes spin at high CPU
zombie Chrome processes after session end
Chrome process tree not terminated on caller exit
signals.review_reason: 资源泄漏问题，直接导致CPU资源持续消耗、机器发热和电池消耗。虽然count=1，但影响真实且明确，归属P1合理。

source_issues.title: Orphaned headless Chrome Helpers spin at high CPU under agent-browser-chrome temp profile
source_issues.evidence: Chrome Helper子进程各自占用85-100% CPU，累计5-6核饱和；进程在agent/session结束后仍存活；OpenClaw daemon重启未自动清理；手动kill后恢复正常。

signals.topic: 守护进程处于半死状态时open命令虚假成功，截图和快照返回前一个URL的旧内容

aliases: open reports success but returns stale content after daemon half-dead state
navigation reported success with wrong page content

source_issues.title: After failed close, subsequent open reports success but returns stale content from prior URL
source_issues.evidence: close失败后open报告'✓ Done'并显示正确标题，但screenshot实际返回旧URL内容；agent读取了无关页面内容，确认为静默数据损坏；相关issue #1336同属一个问题族。

signals.topic: --auto-connect在Chrome权限提示出现时超时过短，自动化工作流无法在时限内完成授权

aliases: auto-connect timeout too short for Chrome permission prompt
--auto-connect fails before user can approve permission dialog
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：自动化agent场景下--auto-connect因授权超时完全失效，核心功能不可用，归属P0。

source_issues.title: `--auto-connect` fails too quickly when Chrome asks for remote debugging permission
source_issues.evidence: 截图显示Chrome远程调试权限提示；auto-connect在约2秒后超时失败；自动化场景下无人值守无法在此时限内完成授权。

signals.topic: Chrome 147在Docker容器中以trap int3崩溃，导致容器内完全无法使用agent-browser
signals.summary: 在Docker容器中运行agent-browser时Chrome以'trap int3'信号崩溃并生成core dump，表现为多次重复崩溃，即使使用--no-sandbox和禁用dev-shm-usage标志也无法避免，导致容器环境下核心功能完全不可用。
aliases: Chrome 147 crashes with trap int3 in Docker
signals.review_reason: Docker容器环境下核心功能完全不可用的阻断性问题，虽然是环境特定的，但错误描述具体且有完整堆栈和core dump证据，归P1。

source_issues.title: Chrome 147.0 crashes with "trap int3" when running in docker
source_issues.evidence: dmesg和coredumpctl显示Chrome 147在容器中trap int3崩溃；SIGTRAP core dump；用户实际无法在Docker环境中执行任何agent-browser命令；已讨论与--enable-unsafe-swiftshader可能的关联。

signals.topic: AI Gateway ByteDance API translation: referenceImages missing role field causes 400 errors
signals.summary: AI Gateway does not add the required per-item role tag when translating referenceImages to ByteDance ModelArk API v2.0 requests, causing 400 errors. Direct @ai-sdk/bytedance provider works correctly.
aliases: AI Gateway bytedance referenceImages role missing
signals.review_reason: Gateway translation bug causes API calls to fail with 400 for users of ByteDance seedance-2.0 with referenceImages — a real functional breakage in a core API path. Users must bypass the Gateway to work around the issue.

source_issues.title: ai-gateway: bytedance/seedance-2.0 + providerOptions.bytedance.referenceImages fails upstream with "role must be specified for image contents"
source_issues.evidence: User reports 400 error from ByteDance ModelArk API when using referenceImages through the Gateway; direct provider works correctly. Root cause is missing role field in gateway's translation layer for v2.0 model family.

signals.topic: Cerebras provider: tools + structured output causes finishReason=tool-call instead of stop
signals.summary: When using both tools and structured output with Cerebras, finishReason is 'tool-call' instead of 'stop', raising a runtime error when using the output and blocking the combined feature set.
signals.review_reason: Users combining tools and structured output with Cerebras get a runtime error on the response — blocks a common agentic pattern. The finishReason mismatch causes the SDK to reject valid-looking outputs.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/cerebras] Cerebras does not work with tools + structured output

signals.topic: Turbopack ISR SSG prerender silently produces incomplete RSC payload causing empty/hydration-skeleton pages in production (21-hour outage documented)
signals.summary: Next.js 16 + Turbopack + ISR (revalidate + generateStaticParams) silently truncates the RSC streaming payload at build time. signals.review_reason: P0: same root cause (Turbopack build-time SSG prerender with ISR truncates RSC streaming), two independent reporters, 21-hour documented production outage, broken cache locked into Vercel edge, build reports success while users see empty pages — this is a silent, production-only failure mode with no build-time signal.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Next.js 16 + turbopack: silent incomplete RSC payload on build-time SSG prerender with generateStaticParams + revalidate (page-content dependent)

source_issues.title: [Bug] Next.js 16 + turbopack + ISR: silent incomplete RSC payload on SSG prerender (generateStaticParams + revalidate, production-only)
