Production-only; isolated repo does NOT reproduce. Hotfix (dynamic=force-dynamic) shipped at cost of ISR benefit.

signals.topic: SWC compile orchestrator deadlock in Next.js 16 causes production builds to hang indefinitely at 0% CPU on ALL platforms (macOS arm64, Linux x86_64, Vercel cloud)
signals.summary: next build hangs deterministically in the SWC compile phase across all Next.js 16 versions (16.0.0 through 16.3.0-canary.21) on both Turbopack and webpack, and on all platforms including macOS arm64, Linux x86_64, and Vercel cloud. The trace file freezes at a byte-exact size (107,831,441 bytes), two worker threads spin at ~100% CPU in a circular wait. This is a production-build blocker for real-world Next.js 16 apps. count=2 (two independent reports).
aliases: next build hangs in SWC compile phase
signals.review_reason: P0: two independent reports, both showing build hangs at SWC compile orchestrator across ALL platforms and ALL 16.x versions. next build is the primary production workflow — blocking it is a critical developer experience failure and effectively locks out all Next.js 16 production deployments for affected app profiles.

source_issues.title: next build hangs indefinitely in SWC compile phase on Next 16 (next dev works) — reproduces on macOS arm64 AND Linux x86_64 (Vercel cloud)
source_issues.evidence: 34+ builds conducted. Hangs on every 16.x version (16.0.0, 16.2.6, 16.3.0-canary.19). Affects both webpack and Turbopack. Reproduces on macOS ARM64, Linux x86_64 (Vercel cloud, 30 cores, 60 GB RAM). .next/trace freezes at byte-exact 107,831,441 bytes. Tokio runtime threads at 1900+ stack frames inside next-swc binary. Circular wait confirmed: orchestrator waits for work; workers wait for assignment. Last known good: next@15.5.18.

source_issues.title: Turbopack next build hangs at 0% CPU on 16.3.0-canary.21 — fingerprint matches PR #92210 (post-fix)
source_issues.evidence: Build enters SWC compile phase then hangs indefinitely at 0% CPU. Parent next-build alive, child compile workers alive but idle. ~4-9 GB RSS retained. Hang rate ~1 in 4 cold-cache builds. next dev works fine.

signals.topic: Per-request IncrementalCache (FileSystemCache) instances leaked via AsyncLocalStorage captured by Node keep-alive sockets causing monotonic heap growth and OOM in standalone mode
signals.summary: Under output:standalone with App Router, per-request IncrementalCache objects are captured by AsyncResource handles attached to Node HTTPS keep-alive sockets via kResourceStore symbol. Per-request caches are never GC'd as long as any keep-alive socket from that request stays alive. Heap grows monotonically until OOM. Regression from 15.5.15 (clean) to 15.5.18 (OOM rate jumps 10x). This is a memory leak that directly causes production crashes.
signals.review_reason: P0: production memory leak causing OOM crashes in production standalone deployments. Heap snapshots with linear growth confirm per-request caches never released. Regression between 15.5.15 and 15.5.18 confirmed with 10x OOM rate increase. This is a direct, measurable production stability issue.

source_issues.title: Per-request IncrementalCache leaked via AsyncLocalStorage captured by keep-alive fetch sockets (15.5.18 standalone)
source_issues.evidence: Heap snapshots 23 min apart: FileSystemCache instances grow 12→17 (one legitimate singleton, 16 per-request leaks). LRUNode instances grow 391→1514. Process heap 200MB→245MB. Regression 15.5.15 (clean) → 15.5.18 (OOM rate 10x jump). Retainer chain: FileSystemCache←.cacheHandler IncrementalCache←.incrementalCache Object←kResourceStore AsyncResource←TLSSocket/TCP←Global handles. Monotonic growth until OOM in production.

signals.topic: Browser back navigation via history causes next/script components to silently fail and not execute in Next.js 16.2.6 (regression)
signals.summary: When navigating back via the browser back button, scripts loaded via next/script are silently disabled and never execute. Users returning to a page via back navigation get broken functionality (analytics, third-party widgets, interactive elements fail silently). Regression introduced in 16.2.6. Affects cacheComponents and Route Handlers.

Silent script failure means analytics, third-party integrations, and interactive components fail without user-visible error — significant user-impacting regression. Count=1 but labeled as regression with clear reproduction path.

source_issues.title: Bug: Scripts disabled due to cache error when navigating back via browser history (Regression) Next JS 16.2.6
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo provided. Steps: navigate away from page, click browser back button, scripts fail silently with no console errors. Regression in 16.2.6. Affects all browsers (Chrome, Edge). Scripts are core to analytics, third-party widgets, and interactive components — silent failure means users unknowingly lose functionality.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker generates corrupted lockfiles causing downstream package manager install to crash in Docker builds

No workaround available to users.

signals.topic: turbo task completion race: subprocesses that escape process group write outputs after turbo signals done, causing dependent tasks to fail with missing modules
signals.summary: Turbo uses process-group-based exit tracking but has a blind spot for descendants that detach from the tracked group before writing declared outputs. This causes a race condition where dependent tasks are scheduled before outputs are on disk, failing CI at ~1.2% rate on Linux and near-deterministically in synthetic test modes.
aliases: process group race condition outputs not ready
dependent tasks scheduled before outputs written
WARNING no output files found race
signals.review_reason: Despite original issue being closed with a fix, the issue explicitly states that intentional-escape modes (detached, double-fork, delayed-pgid) are a separate follow-up not covered by the merged fix. The bug has a confirmed real-world failure rate (~1.2% on Linux CI) affecting builds with detached subprocess patterns common in Node.js CLI tools. Each failure blocks dependent tasks, which is a core pipeline correctness failure. The count is 1 because only one source issue exists, but the issue self-documents the gap in the fix and the real-world reproduction evidence is strong.

source_issues.title: Task signaled complete before subprocess writes declared outputs when descendants leave the tracked process group
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced at 99.5-100% rate in synthetic modes (detached/double-fork/delayed-pgid); real-world toolchain reproduces at 1.2% on Linux CI runners; dependent tasks fail with 'Could not resolve' because declared outputs are not yet on disk; fix PR #12790 partially addressed in-group case but intentional-escape modes remain unfixed per the issue itself

turbo cannot resolve workspaces pnpm v11

signals.topic: Cache returns stale results for format/lint tasks when source file content is restored between runs
signals.summary: Turbo caches format/lint task outputs even when the source file hash has changed and was subsequently restored to its original hash. This causes turbo to incorrectly report cached results, skipping actual formatting/linting and producing incorrect CI results.
aliases: incorrect cache hit after file modification restore
turbo cache format skipped wrong results
signals.review_reason: Turbo's caching mechanism produces incorrect (silent) results by returning cached output when source file content changed and was restored. This is a correctness bug — tasks that should run are skipped, and CI pipelines get false-positive results. The hash update is confirmed but cache still hits, indicating a fundamental flaw in the caching logic around transient file changes.

source_issues.title: Turbo only cache files at the start of a command, resulting in erroneous format/linting cache hit

signals.topic: SIGINT signal not forwarded to child processes when script-shell is sh, breaking graceful shutdown for Windows users
signals.summary: When script-shell defaults to sh (common on Windows), turbo does not forward SIGINT to child processes. This prevents user code from receiving the interrupt signal and triggering graceful shutdown sequences, unlike when script-shell is bash.
aliases: graceful shutdown broken on Windows sh shell
signals.review_reason: Windows users are disproportionately affected since sh is the default script-shell on Windows via npm. This breaks a critical developer experience pattern (graceful shutdown on Ctrl+C), which is commonly needed for dev servers and long-running processes. While not a build pipeline blocker, it represents a significant DX regression for Windows users that has no straightforward workaround.

source_issues.title: SIGINT is not forwarded properly when script-shell=sh
source_issues.evidence: With script-shell=bash, pressing Ctrl+C triggers graceful shutdown (SIGINT received by user code); with script-shell=sh, SIGINT is never forwarded to child processes and graceful shutdown is skipped entirely; Windows users cannot use bash by default and are blocked from graceful shutdown patterns
